Americold Realty Trust raised its full-year earnings outlook Thursday after reporting higher third-quarter revenue and improved warehouse margins, while a one-time gain from its joint venture with EQT drove a sharp swing to profit.
The temperature-controlled logistics company (NYSE: COLD ) based in Atlanta reported net income of $683.4 million, or $2.38 per diluted share, for the quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with a loss of $11.4 million, or 4 cents per share, a year earlier. The turnaround primarily reflected a $714.1 million after-tax gain tied to the contribution of real estate assets to the joint venture, rather than a comparable increase in recurring earnings.
Revenue rose 4.2% to $691.6 million from $663.7 million. Adjusted funds from operations, or AFFO, totaled $101.3 million, compared with $100.7 million a year earlier, while AFFO per diluted share remained unchanged at 35 cents.
Americold increased its 2026 AFFO forecast to $1.31 to $1.33 per share, its second consecutive increase in the full-year outlook. Its previous range was $1.26 to $1.32 per share.
Chief Executive Rob Chambers in a statement attributed the quarter’s operating improvement to gains in occupancy, the volume of goods moving through facilities and pricing, alongside lower selling, general and administrative costs.
“While the operating environment remains challenging, our efforts are yielding visible results, and we have seen a multi-quarter improvement in key metrics across the business,” Chambers said.
Same-store revenue in the global warehouse segment increased 5.7%, or 4.9% excluding currency movements. Same-store net operating income rose 6%, while the same-store services margin expanded to 15.9% from 13.6%.
Companywide core earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization rose 7.5% to $159.4 million. The corresponding margin increased to 23% from 22.3%.
Revenue growth also reflected higher transportation services revenue, favorable currency movements and $13.1 million in joint-venture management fees and reimbursed costs. Those gains were partially offset by the transfer of warehouse properties into the EQT partnership.
The EQT transaction, which closed Aug. 31, was central to both the reported profit surge and Americold’s deleveraging. The company said the deal enabled it to reduce outstanding debt by $1.15 billion and lowered its net leverage ratio by a full turn.
Americold retained a 30% stake in the partnership, which owns 12 temperature-controlled warehouse facilities in North America, and continues to serve as day-to-day property manager. Chambers said the arrangement also establishes a development partner for future growth opportunities.
At quarter-end, Americold had approximately $3.3 billion in net debt and $950.4 million in liquidity. Net debt stood at about 6.2 times pro forma core EBITDA, or approximately 6.3 times on a measure incorporating its proportionate share of partially owned entities.
Despite the substantial increase in reported net income, recurring earnings measures were mixed. AFFO per share held steady, while core funds from operations declined to $66.9 million, or 23 cents per diluted share, from $81.7 million, or 29 cents per share, a year earlier.
Why it matters: Americold’s warehouse business is stabilizing while a major debt reduction strengthens its financial footing, though unchanged adjusted EPS shows operating recovery remains gradual.

A $4.5 billion expansion at the Bagdad mine in northwestern Arizona would more than double the amount of ore the site can mine and process. Freeport-McMoRan said Nov. 4 that its board approved the project and that it expects the expanded mine to begin producing in mid-2030.
What’s Related
Freeport expects the project to add about 225 million pounds of copper and 12 million pounds of molybdenum a year. That would bring long-term annual output to more than 400 million pounds of copper and 20 million pounds of molybdenum. Freeport says Bagdad would become the country’s second-largest copper mine, behind its Morenci mine, also in Arizona.
“We are pleased to proceed with the Bagdad expansion, an important step in advancing Freeport’s U.S. copper growth strategy,” said Kathleen Quirk, Freeport’s president and CEO. The company is moving ahead with engineering, planning equipment purchases, and preparing the site for construction, which it expects to last about three and a half years.
How Bagdad will process more ore
The biggest addition is a new concentrator that separates valuable minerals from crushed rock. Freeport expects it to add about 115,000 metric tons of daily processing capacity. The project also calls for a new primary crusher, a conveyor to move material across the site, and new water and power lines.
The mine will rely on driverless haul trucks to move more material. Freeport completed Bagdad’s fleet conversion in 2025 and says it was the first major U.S. mine to switch entirely to autonomous haulage . During the transition, the company said many former drivers moved into jobs operating the shovels that load the trucks.
Bagdad has been operating since 1945. Freeport says the mine has about 2.6 billion metric tons of ore in its reserves and more than 80 years of reserve life based on current estimates.
More than 4,000 new jobs
Freeport expects to spend about 20% of the project budget in 2027 and another 30% to 35% in 2028, with the rest coming in 2029 and 2030. The company said rising costs could push the final price above its current estimate. It projects more than 4,000 direct and indirect jobs during construction.
Once the expansion is running, Freeport expects its long-term cash cost per pound of copper at Bagdad to fall about 20% after accounting for molybdenum sales. The company estimates the project would break even at a copper price of about $4 a pound, assuming molybdenum sells for $20 a pound.

Posted By: FREDERIC TOMESCO November 5, 2026
B2Gold (TSX: BTO; NYSE-A: BTG) cut its annual cost forecast and said repairs and upgrades at the fire-damaged crushing circuit of its Goose mine in Nunavut cleared a key production bottleneck.
Vancouver-based B2Gold lowered its 2026 all-in sustaining cost guidance to $2,230–$2,410 (C$3,122–C$3,374) an oz. from $2,370–$2,550, a reduction of about 6% at the midpoint. The annual production target remains unchanged at 820,000–920,000 oz., the company said late Wednesday in its third-quarter report .
“Goose execution continues to derisk,” Jefferies mining analyst Fahad Tariq said Wednesday in a note. With about 73% of the company’s 2026 output target already achieved as of Sept. 30, “we see limited risk to achieving production guidance, while lower [cost] guidance is encouraging.”
The improved outlook rests on B2Gold’s other mines, leaving Goose as the main test of its operational recovery. The Nunavut operation needs about 74,000 oz. in the fourth quarter, up 86% from the third, just to reach the bottom of its annual production range. Its repaired crusher must now deliver through the Arctic winter.
B2Gold’s adjusted third-quarter earnings of 14¢ a share exceeded the 12¢ consensus cited by Jefferies and National Bank Financial. The miner produced 193,321 oz. gold in the period, generating $48 million in quarterly free cash flow following the completion of its prepaid gold sales contracts in June.
Shares of B2Gold rose 0.8% to C$7.21 Thursday morning in Toronto, valuing the company at about C$9.5 billion ($6.8 billion). The stock has traded between C$5.02 and C$8.60 in the past year.
Goose struggles
Since first gold was poured in June 2025, Goose “has struggled to maintain mill throughput, mostly due to crusher issues,” BMO Capital Markets analyst Brian Quast wrote in an Oct. 5 site-visit report.
The April fire compounded those difficulties, forcing B2Gold to rely on mobile crushing equipment while repairing the permanent plant. During the recent analyst visit, the mobile crusher was being enclosed to support more consistent operation through the Nunavut winter.
Goose produced 39,973 oz. gold in the third quarter, up from about 12,900 oz. in the previous period, but the site’s all-in sustaining costs remained elevated at $4,816 an ounce. National Bank Financial analyst Don DeMarco attributed the high figure partly to gold sales lagging production, alongside spending on fire repairs, mobile crushing and deferred work.
B2Gold continues to expect to produce 170,000–200,000 oz. at Goose this year, it said Wednesday. The Nunavut mine needs roughly 74,000 oz. in the fourth quarter to reach the bottom of that range, making sustained operation of the repaired circuit critical, DeMarco said.
Other operations
The lower group cost outlook comes from B2Gold’s other operations. Strong year-to-date production at Masbate in the Philippines and Otjikoto in Namibia, together with lower royalties at Fekola in Mali, supported the reduction. Goose’s cost guidance is unchanged at $2,670–$2,970 an oz., with results expected near the upper end.
As a result, execution at Goose remains “the main near-term cost watchpoint,” Tariq wrote.
Beyond Goose, B2Gold’s Fekola Regional operation offers another source of growth. Waste stripping began in October following receipt of the Menankoto exploitation permit. First ore at the Fekola plant is expected early next year, subject to completion of a toll-milling agreement.
“Successful delivery of the year-end Goose ramp and first regional ore at Fekola should increasingly shift attention toward the company’s higher production and improved cash-flow profile beyond the current transition year,” DeMarco said.

Caserones mine. ( Image courtesy of Caserones | Lundin Mining. )
Posted By: Cecilia Jamasmie November 5, 2026
Lundin Mining (TSX: LUN) has lowered its annual copper production forecast for the second time since August as snowmelt continues to disrupt its Caserones mine in Chile, despite stronger-than-expected quarterly cash flow.
The miner cut Caserones’ target to 105,000–115,000 tonnes from 120,000–130,000 tonnes, reducing company-wide guidance to 285,000–310,000 tonnes from 300,000–325,000 tonnes. The mine began the year targeting 130,000–140,000 tonnes before an August reduction .
“Importantly, these are deferred tonnes rather than lost production, and we expect to see a recovery in operational performance through 2027,” president and CEO Jack Lundin said in the company’s quarterly results , released Wednesday.
Reaching the midpoint of the reduced forecast requires about 78,000 tonnes in the fourth quarter, a 25% increase from the third, BMO Capital Markets analyst Matthew Murphy said Thursday. That puts pressure on Caserones to recover while Candelaria maintains strong grades and Chapada delivers steady output, as Lundin approaches a major investment decision at Vicuña.
Lundin shares traded 10% weaker at C$28.48 Thursday morning in Toronto, giving the company a market value of about C$24.3 billion.
Storm disruption
Power outages caused by severe winter storms halted Caserones for about 30 days during the third quarter, including time needed to thaw flotation equipment and restart mills. Subsequent snowmelt has reduced haulage rates and restricted ore deliveries into the fourth quarter.
The mine is about 125 km southeast of Copiapó in Chile’s Atacama region.
Company-wide copper production reached 62,610 tonnes in the three months to Sept. 30, matching BMO’s forecast but missing the 68,000-tonne consensus estimate, Murphy said. Gold output of 36,763 oz. exceeded his estimate and roughly matched consensus.
Caserones’ annual cash cost guidance remains $2.15–$2.35 per lb., following an increase in August. Consolidated guidance remains $1.95–$2.15 per lb.
Candelaria’s copper production rose 13% from the second quarter, while Chapada in Brazil recorded its highest quarterly copper and gold output of the year.
Cash-flow cushion
Free cash flow reached $312 million (C$436 million), exceeding BMO’s $14-million forecast and consensus of $219 million. Capital spending was lower than expected, while a $61-million working-capital release boosted operating cash flow, Murphy said.
Desjardins analyst Bryce Adams described the results as mixed, with lower operating costs and stronger realized copper prices helping offset weaker sales volumes. Adjusted earnings of 32¢ a share exceeded his 28¢ forecast, but the reduced annual copper production range fell below his estimate of 314,000 tonnes. He maintained a buy rating and C$45 target.
Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization of $648 million also exceeded forecasts. However, that measure excluded $58 million in Caserones fixed overhead costs that BMO had included in its estimate, he said.
Lundin ended September with net cash of $237 million. It also lowered annual capital spending guidance by $50 million to $980 million, including a $20-million reduction in sustaining spending at Caserones.
Vicuña decision
Lundin is targeting a year-end investment decision at Vicuña , its equal partnership with BHP (ASX, LSE, NYSE: BHP). The project combines the Josemaría and Filo del Sol copper-gold deposits along the Argentina-Chile border.
The venture has secured a provincial agreement with San Juan and approval for a high-voltage powerline connecting the project to Argentina’s grid. Engineering, financing arrangements and an updated first-stage capital estimate remain part of the work towards sanctioning.
At Chapada, construction of an additional ball mill is about 15% complete, with commissioning targeted for late 2027.
The Vicuña investment decision, project optimization and capital-cost update are the key upcoming events for Lundin’s shares, Murphy said. BMO maintained an outperform rating and C$49 target.

Dealer Sells a Ford Mustang Shelby GT350 That Really Was Driven by an Old Lady to the Grocery Store
15 photos
Photo: Justin SVT | YouTube & Apex Motors
Only driven by an old lady to the church and to the grocery store. That is one of the most common clichés when it comes to selling cars on the used car market. However, in this case, it might very well be true. This 2017 Ford Mustang Shelby GT350 hit the market after being driven around by a senior lady driver.
It may look gorgeous from ten feet away, but come closer and you'll see that it's been through thick and thin and everything in between. Justin of Justin SVT YouTube channel spotted the car in the parking lot of a dealership in Murray, Utah, and instantly realized he had seen and filmed it before, driving around in a small town in Southern Utah. At the time, it was driven around by an old lady and was in pretty rough shape. She almost never washed it, as Justin used to see it filthy and neglected.
It looked like the senior lady driver couldn't care less about the visual flaws of her 2017 Ford Mustang Shelby GT350 . She had lost the factory keyhole cover along the way, and the original black racing stripes on the aluminum hood and trunk lid were heavily sun-faded and weathered from being exposed to the brutal Utah desert sun.
Furthermore, the clear Paint Protection Film on the front end was old and had started to peel off the body panels. The GT350 looked not like an exclusive model that was worth being pampered, but like a neglected economy commuter.
Photo: Justin SVT | YouTube And the list of flaws was far from over. A scratch running down the rear driver-side quarter panel by the wheel well is still visible on the car sitting in the parking lot of Apex Motors. At one point, while the woman was driving it, the rear window on the right side was completely shattered, despite the presence of the aftermarket plastic window louvers.
The dealership tried to erase the GT350's battle scars. It removed the louvers and replaced the missing cover on the driver’s door keyhole, but a slight difference in paint tone is visible in Justin’s latest video as proof of a hard past life.
Justin recalls a mileage of roughly 42,000 miles on the blue Mustang, which now comes with a resonator delete, making the flat-plane crank V8 sound incredibly loud, but Justin points out that it is a pretty sloppy welding job. However, it definitely doesn’t sound like a car that would be driven by grandma.
First and foremost, it is what is under the hood that would scare most seniors away. The 2017 Ford Mustang Shelby GT350 is powered by the 5.2-liter flat-plane crank Voodoo V8 engine with naturally aspirated firepower.
Photo: Justin SVT | YouTube The V8 pumps out 526 horsepower (533 metric horsepower) and 429 pound-feet (582 Newton meters) of torque. That is what makes it rocket from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 4.1 seconds, or just 3.9 with a one-foot rollout. It runs the quarter mile in 12.4 seconds with a trap speed of 117 mph (188 kph) and tops out at 180 mph (290 kph). A Tremec six-speed manual transmission puts the power down through the rear wheels.
The Mustang Shelby GT350 is finished in the head-turning Lightning Blue Metallic (paint code N6), introduced for the 2017 model year to replace the deeper Deep Impact Blue. However, the paint has started to lose its shine. The Mustang rides on 19-inch multi-spoke aluminum alloy wheels finished in Ebony Black.
The interior doesn't look half as bad as the exterior. The 2017 Shelby GT350 came standard with heavily bolstered Recaro sport bucket seats upholstered in a mix of Ebony cloth and Miko Alcantara inserts, while the steering wheel in leather and Alcantara sports a 12 o’clock marker and frames the speedometer scaled up to 200 mph, the tachometer with a redline starting at 8,250 rpm, along with gauges indicating oil pressure and temperature.
The nine-year-old GT350, equipped with the Track Pack, was listed for $45,995 and eventually sold, as it is no longer listed on the dealer's platform. Justin has already checked, and it comes with a clean title, but he has no idea how the dealership acquired it. Hopefully, the buyer will fix all the visual flaws that it comes with, along with mechanical issues, if any, and will treat it as it deserves.
Photo: Justin SVT | YouTube & Apex Motors Hopefully, the previous owner did maintenance work on time to keep the Voodoo V8 in a perfectly functional state. Otherwise, that poor V8 under the hood is a ticking bomb. According to Ford, it requires oil changes every 3,000 miles or less.
However, considering that Justin used to spot the car always filthy and the previous owner didn’t even bother to replace a broken window, it is very unlikely she actually followed the Ford-recommended maintenance plan.
Ford produced only 7,115 Mustang Shelby GT350s for 2017, with 6,173 standard units, like the car listed by Apex Motors, and 942 track-focused GT350Rs. Out of all 2017 models, only 1,037 cars were painted Lightning Blue, which makes the model incredibly rare.
The average price for a standard 2017 Ford Mustang Shelby GT350 sits at approximately $58,300 nowadays. However, it all comes down to condition and mileage. At over 40,000 miles, this car hasn't exactly been a garage queen.
So don't be sorry if it’s not you the one who took it home for a price under the market average. I believe you just dodged a bullet!

The scramble is over. Carriers and owner-operators who spent the past few years chasing build slots, paying inflated prices for used units and taking whatever iron they could find are now facing a different problem: plenty of options and very little margin for a bad decision. Lead times have stabilized, used pricing has found a floor and freight rates are rewarding only the operators who keep costs tight.
Werner sees that shift from an unusual vantage point. Through Werner Fleet Sales, the company sells retired tractors directly to carriers and owner-operators, which puts it in daily contact with the people deciding whether to buy new, buy used or hold on to what they already have. Its read on the market is a sober one. According to John Paynter, general sales manager at Werner Fleet Sales, “the Class 8 truck and trailer market is in a disciplined realignment phase following years of supply chain volatility, freight rate normalization and elevated interest rates.”
A calmer supply picture, a costlier truck
The most visible change is the end of the emergency. Original equipment manufacturer lead times have stabilized, Paynter said, “eliminating the emergency supply shortages seen in prior years.” That does not mean new trucks have gotten easier to afford. Paynter noted that acquisition costs “remain historically high due to advanced technology, safety suites and regulatory emissions engineering.”
The secondary market has changed even more. After the “hyper-inflated valuations of 2021–2022,” used trucks now trade in what Paynter calls a “buyer-centric, value-driven market.” Pricing has bottomed and stabilized, but buyers are not simply grabbing the cheapest unit on the lot. They are, in Paynter’s words, “highly selective, prioritizing well-maintained, low-mileage, late-model units over older, high-risk assets.”
The effect on behavior is easy to see. “Both large carriers and independent operators are avoiding speculative expansion,” Paynter said. Purchases are being tied to planned replacement cycles, fuel efficiency and lower maintenance costs rather than to a bet that freight is about to snap back.
Three variables behind every purchase decision
“Major out-of-frame overhaul costs or un-budgeted emissions system failures can bankrupt a small carrier,” Paynter said. That is the risk hanging over every equipment decision an owner-operator or small fleet makes, and it explains why buyers weigh the higher capital cost of new or late-model units covered by factory warranties against the cheaper price of older trucks that carry elevated breakdown risk.
Debt service sharpens the tradeoff. With interest rates still above pre-2022 levels, Paynter said, “high monthly payments on expensive new trucks can severely compress operating margins.” The freight market adds pressure from the other side. With freight rates “demanding lean operations,” operators are choosing equipment with lower operating expense profiles rather than taking on heavy fixed debt.
Put together, the purchase price is only one input. Monthly cash flow, repair exposure and spot-market reality all shape whether a buyer goes new, goes used or holds on to the truck they already own.
Why buying direct changes the equation
Werner Fleet Sales sells its retired equipment directly to buyers rather than liquidating exclusively through wholesale auctions. The company points to several advantages, starting with a clean ownership story. Direct-sale units have been owned, operated and serviced exclusively within Werner’s nationwide network by ASE-certified technicians following preventive maintenance schedules.
That history is paired with a reconditioning process. Paynter said units go through a 150-point inspection and receive brand-new tires, brake refurbishments that meet or exceed DOT standards, and professional cabin detailing before delivery.
The third benefit is cost. Demand for fleet-direct purchases has increased, according to Paynter, as buyers look to eliminate auction markup fees and gain confidence in verifiable maintenance records. In a market where buyers are wary of older, high-risk assets, a documented one-owner service history carries real weight.
Financing is the biggest lever
If one factor is shaping the pace of equipment deals more than any other, Paynter said it is financing. In his words, “financing is currently the single largest lever in equipment transaction velocity.”
Higher rates have stretched the loan horizon. Where 36- to 48-month terms were once standard for used equipment, Paynter said 48- to 60-month terms are increasingly being used to keep monthly debt service manageable. Lenders, meanwhile, are asking for more. Paynter said they “require stronger credit profiles, higher down payments, and verified operational cash reserves.”
Residual values are part of the same conversation. Both lenders and buyers are applying conservative estimates, preferring units with established market demand and strong trade-in values at 500,000 to 600,000 miles. For owner-operators, that makes the question of what a truck will be worth at the end of a loan just as important as what it costs at the start.
Spec’ing for savings and retention
Spec decisions have shifted toward measurable operating savings and driver retention over the past year or two, according to Paynter. Four priorities stand out.
Fuel economy: Paynter pointed to growing emphasis on automated manual transmissions, predictive cruise control, optimized axle ratios and full fairing aerodynamic packages, all aimed at reducing variable operating costs per mile.
Safety technology: Buyers are prioritizing advanced driver assistance systems, including collision mitigation, lane departure warnings and active braking, to lower insurance premiums and reduce liability risk.
Uptime and diagnostics: Paynter said demand is growing for telematics integration, remote engine diagnostics and over-the-air updates that speed up repair shop turnaround and help avoid road calls.
Driver comfort: Raised-roof sleepers, double bunks, factory-installed inverters and quiet cab insulation are being treated as investments in retention and fatigue reduction.
New or used? Run the numbers first
For an owner-operator weighing the two paths, Paynter’s advice starts with arithmetic. “Calculate the monthly difference between a new truck payment and a late-model used truck payment,” Paynter said. If a late-model used truck saves $800 to $1,200 per month, that difference can build “a crucial cash emergency reserve fund.”
Paynter also pointed to what he calls the sweet spot: a three- to four-year-old, fleet-maintained unit with 350,000 to 450,000 miles. Those trucks, Paynter said, “have already absorbed the steepest curve of depreciation while retaining factory warranty eligibility.”
The last piece of advice is about discipline. “Never buy on appearance alone,” Paynter said, recommending full oil and filter analysis, verified maintenance logs and recent DOT inspection reports before any money changes hands.
A total cost of ownership mindset
Werner frames equipment through a total cost of ownership model, which it expresses as a simple formula: depreciation, debt service, fuel, maintenance and insurance, divided by total annual miles. The goal is to see a truck as a cost per mile over its life rather than a purchase price on a given day.
That thinking shapes how Werner manages its own fleet. The company trades out tractors before maintenance cost curves spike, typically around the 400,000- to 500,000-mile mark, so secondary buyers receive “a reliable asset with remaining useful life.” Routine oil sampling, overhead adjustments and tire wear tracking are meant to protect resale value and operating efficiency over the long run.
Fuel efficiency is the most direct way to see the model at work. Paynter said improving from 7.0 mpg to 8.2 mpg can yield thousands of dollars in annual operating savings, which is why it encourages buyers to treat spec choices as part of the cost equation instead of an add-on.
From company driver to owner-operator
Werner’s equipment programs also provide a pathway for drivers who want to go into business for themselves. Drivers making that move can use Werner Fleet Sales to find vetted, late-model Freightliner Cascadias, Kenworth T680s or Peterbilt 579s with fuel-efficient specs. Through carrier and driver reward networks, qualifying drivers can access purchase discounts, in-house financing guidance and leased-on freight opportunities.
The questions drivers ask before making the jump are practical ones, according to Paynter. What are my true fixed monthly costs, such as truck payment, insurance and permits, compared with variable costs like fuel and a maintenance reserve? Is there remaining factory engine and aftertreatment warranty coverage on the unit? And what is my access to reliable, consistent freight density to cover debt service during market dips?
That last question may be the most important. A truck payment is fixed. Freight is not.
What Werner is watching
Looking ahead, Paynter identified three trends Werner is tracking closely.
The first is regulation. The company is preparing for upcoming EPA rules and state-level zero-emission or low-emission transition schedules, which “directly impact future acquisition costs and residual values.”
The second is trailer utilization. Werner is watching trailer-to-tractor ratios, the balance between dry van and temperature-controlled demand, and the expansion of trailer tracking technology.
The third is capacity. Werner is tracking the exit of unviable spot-market capacity and its eventual effect on freight rate recovery, which Paynter expects “will signal the next major equipment re-fleeting cycle.”
Until that cycle arrives, the playbook is a patient one: buy for the miles you can cover, finance for the cash flow you can sustain, and choose equipment with a documented history. In a market that has stopped rewarding speculation, the buyers coming out ahead are the ones who treat a truck as a cost per mile rather than a status symbol.

PUGET SOUND, Wash. (April 14, 2017) - The Seawolf-class fast-attack submarine USS Jimmy Carter (SSN 23) transits the Hood Canal as the boat returns home to Naval Base Kitsap-Bangor. Jimmy Carter is the last and most advanced of the Seawolf-class attack submarines, which are all homeported at Naval Base Kitsap. (U.S. Navy photo by Lt. Cmdr. Michael Smith/Released)
PARIS — Fairbanks Morse Defense ( FMD ) is poised to conduct repairs on the US Navy’s three Seawolf-class submarines, as the company expands its submarine maintenance footprint.
FMD’s preparations to repair the submarines come just after US Naval Sea Systems Command awarded the firm an approximately $100 million follow-on contract in October to conduct Emergency Diesel Generator (EDG) overhauls on six aging Los Angeles- and Ohio-class submarines, part of a broader effort to extend the vessels’ service lives by as many as 14 years.
The Seawolf-class submarines, the first of which entered the fleet in 1997, could be next in line for maintenance. Fairbanks Morse Defense CEO George Whittier confirmed that the company is now in discussions with the Navy about conducting maintenance on the Seawolf subs. He expects work on those vessels to begin after the Los Angeles- and Ohio-class submarine overhauls, which are expected to wrap up in the late 2020s.
“We’re going to end up doing overhauls on those as well, right?” Whittier told Breaking Defense at the Euronaval defense exposition in Paris about the Seawolf class. “Because again, they’re 25, 30-year-old boats, right? So all of that’s going to be coming.”
Submarine maintenance delays have perpetually been a thorny issue for the Navy. For example, the Government Accountability Office issued a report in August that found public shipyards, which perform maintenance on nuclear-powered vessels like submarines, completed only 11 percent of submarine maintenance periods on schedule.
Additionally, the Navy is facing questions about whether it can deliver the Columbia-class submarine by a 2028 target . As a result, the new contract to extend the lives of the Los Angeles- and Ohio-class submarines tackles “the geopolitical risk of a post-2029 submarine deficit” stemming from potential delays in Columbia-class and Virginia-class submarine construction, as well as the decommissioning of other aging vessels, FMD said in a news release in October.
The October contract builds upon a previous NAVSEA award under which FMD completed emergency diesel generator overhauls on two Ohio-class submarines, and one Los Angeles-class submarine.
Keith Haasl, FMD president of Services and Technology, said in an October statement, that the contract reflects growing investment in submarine capabilities by the United States and its allies, as well as by competitors Russia and China, which are expanding and modernizing their own fleets.
“Because the timely delivery of critical components dictates fleet availability, we are moving quickly to scale our capabilities,” Haasl said. “Our work with the Navy actively demonstrates principles of rapid submarine maintenance and overhaul that we can share with allies, so we can ensure operationally ready submarines faster.”
FMD is also looking to accelerate its Pit Stop maintenance program, an initiative inspired by NASCAR and Formula One that uses pre-staged original equipment manufacturer parts, standardized procedures and the company’s robotic welding platform to reduce repair timelines.
The company has completed roughly 10 Pit Stops with the Navy over the past five years, and is targeting another 10 in 2027, Whittier said. Those 10 planned Pit Stops next year will cover surface ships .
Separately, FMD also announced in October that it has begun expanding its subsidiary facility, the Bird-Johnson Propeller Company in Pascagoula, Miss., in an effort to double its naval propulsion system capacity. The expansion includes a $27 million investment from the Navy — funded largely through Australia’s US Submarine Industrial Base contribution as part of the AUKUS Pillar I agreement .

GM Recalls Chevy Express and GMC Savana Vans for Potential Steering Gear Assembly Issue
9 photos
Photo: GMC
As fate would have it, General Motors now has to fix a problem it thought it had already remedied. The largest manufacturer among Detroit's Big Three is aware of certain vans fitted with steering gear assemblies that may contain a loose nut. General Motors already recalled these vans under campaign 26V399 earlier this year, but alas, the previous recall missed a bunch of suspect gear assemblies.
The root cause behind the second recall, which is referred to as 26V718 by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, is the supplier. A malfunctioning part sensor at Nexteer Automotive's facility allowed some assemblies to pass inspection without the subject nut being properly torqued.
GM launched the first campaign, which covered 51 suspect steering gear assembly serial numbers, in June 2026. Dealers were instructed to inspect all vehicles against the provided list of serial numbers, replace matching assemblies, and close non-matching vans after inspection.
A General Motors quality manager then filed a report in September 2026 after a dealer found a loose nut in a 2025 model year Chevrolet Express, namely a vehicle that had already been inspected and closed under the prior campaign. The subsequent investigation matched the serial number to the disposition list, with GM and Nexteer determining that up to 108 serial numbers had been incorrectly omitted. How come?
General Motors believed all those suspect parts were still contained by Nexteer. Affected vehicle identification numbers are now searchable on the NHTSA 's portal, Chevy's website, and GMC's website for Savana owners. GM has instructed Chevrolet and GMC dealers to inspect serial numbers against the expanded list and, if there's a match, replace the steering gear assembly at no charge to affected customers.
Photo: GMC Nexteer's replacement steering gears have nuts torqued to specification. The condition was apparently contained at the supplier back in May 2026, and vans built after June 1, 2026, feature properly fastened nuts. For extra peace of mind, GM also updated the service bulletin for 26V399 to add the missing serial numbers.
GM says that notification letters are scheduled to be mailed on December 14, 2026. Until then, the easiest way to tell if your van is potentially affected is to use the aforementioned VIN lookup tools.
The second recall covers 2025 and 2026 models, with production dates ranging from January 21, 2025, through June 1, 2026. Both full-size vans are primarily made at Wentzville Assembly in Missouri. Cutaway van chassis variants, meanwhile, hail from the International Motors plant in Springfield, Ohio.
Wentzville is the perfect place for the full-size vans because it's optimized for such vehicles and body-on-frame designs. In addition, Wentzville also makes the Colorado and Canyon mid-size trucks. For the base-chassis variants, which are meant for conversions like ambulances and box trucks, International Motors is the right partner, as it is specialized in commercial vehicles and medium-duty trucks.

Advocates are sounding the alarm on social media as they learn from their doctors that Novartis has received reports of tumors in patients who have been treated with the spinal muscular atrophy gene therapy.
Novartis’ Zolgensma has faced its share of controversy. Now, the spinal muscular atrophy gene therapy is making the rounds on social media again, as patient advocates sound the alarm over tumors possibly related to the product.
“Just wanted to give people a heads-up, just got back from a neurologist appointment where we were informed that Zolgensma has been linked to two cases of kids developing tumors with seven more cases that are likely tied to it,” Dustin Brondyke, who said he has a child with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), wrote Wednesday on LinkedIn in a post shared by patient advocate Carolyn Philstrom. “Novartis, the pharmaceutical company is withholding information on some of the cases and is doing a ‘tiered rollout’ of information instead of publishing the findings,” Brondyke added.
In communications shared with BioSpace by Philstrom on Thursday morning, another parent of a child with SMA “came to know about this tumor issue last week.” The patient’s appointment was Nov. 4. “It seems Novartis has written to everyone at the same time,” the anonymous parent wrote. “So far, the two confirmed cases seems to have happened 18-60 months after dosing.”
Since Zolgensma was approved in 2019 for children under two years old with SMA, nine tumors have been reported in patients previously treated with the therapy, Novartis confirmed with BioSpace in a Thursday morning statement.
“Of those, two cases to date have shown evidence of vector integration into the DNA of the patients. In both cases, the patients underwent treatment and continue to be monitored,” the spokesperson said. “The potential risk of tumors due to vector integration is currently included in the Zolgensma prescribing information.”
Indeed, Zolgensma’s label includes a warning about the theoretical risk of tumorigenicity stemming from the gene therapy’s adeno-associated viral (AAV) vector. Seven reports of tumors have not been causally linked to the therapy.
As of Thursday, more than 6,000 patients have been treated with Zolgensma across clinical trials, managed access programs and commercial treatment, Novartis said in its email. “As part of Novartis’ ongoing commitment to monitoring the safety of our medicines, we continually evaluate new safety information and assess all reported cases.”
SMA Europe acknowledged the reports in a statement published Thursday morning.
“We understand that the relevant regulatory authorities are actively involved and are currently assessing the available evidence and determining what further steps may be needed,” the organization said. “SMA Europe has also been informed about the situation through confidential channels and have made clear to Novartis that the SMA community now needs timely public communication.”
Zolgensma uses an AAV vector to deliver a transgene encoding the human survival motor neuron (SMN) protein, which is essential for motor neuron function. SMA is caused by a mutation or deletion in the SMN1 gene.
This is not the first time Zolgensma has come under the microscope for safety concerns. The focus of previous scrutiny, however, had focused on liver-related adverse events. In September 2021, two years after Zolgensma’s approval, an FDA advisory committee was held to discuss both Novartis’ therapy and Spark Therapeutics’ Luxturna, a gene therapy for an inherited retinal disease.
About one-third of the 500 patients who had received Zolgensma at that time had experienced a liver-related adverse event, including one case of serious liver failure, according to FDA documents published at the time, Fierce Biotech reported. A summary of the adcomm meeting concluded that “Benefit-risk evaluations of AAV gene therapy (GT) products should be made on a case-by-case basis.”
The reports of tumors among patients who received Zolgensma come as Novartis is already dealing with safety concerns over its investigational CAR T therapy zolacabtagene autoleucel (zola-cel). Late this summer, it was revealed that the company had paused multiple studies of zola-cel after three patients who received the therapy died from immune effector cell-associated hemophagocytic syndrome.

Honda Has a Taste of the e-MTB World with the RN0 Motor-Assisted Bicycle
97 photos
Photo: Honda
If I am to be generous, I could say there are around 20 major motorcycle makers in the world right now. Of that, only a fraction are also involved in making bicycles, be them powered in one way or another, or simply pedal-operated. Technically speaking, Honda isn't one of them. Or wasn't, as this week, during the EICMA show in Milan, it presented something special.
Enter the RN0, an electric mountain bike (e-MTB) that marks the Japanese company's formal entry into a realm it tried before, but never decided to commit to, and its first motor-assisted bicycle. Built together with Germany-based specialist ROTWILD , it is supposed to open up a whole new chapter in the company's history.
The bike is built around a carbon monocoque frame that was inspired by the world of motorcycles, and uses the bike maker's gullwing swingarm and linkage system. It is propped on DT Swiss wheels sized 29 inches at the front and 27.5 inches at the rear, with Schwalbe rubber making the connection to the ground.
A suspension system supplied by Fox, comprised of a fork at the front and a shock at the rear, is what aids riders when moving over difficult terrain, while braking power comes courtesy of hardware supplied by Shimano.
This being an electric bicycle and all, it does need to have the proper powertrain. For the task at hand, Honda went for a Shimano drive unit and a removable 720Wh battery. The motor fitted on the RN0 is potent enough to generate 750W of power and 100 Nm of torque.
The 12-speed Shimano Deore XT Di2 drivetrain that was included in the design is made in such a way as to optimize gear selection and traction no matter if the bike is climbing or descending.
Honda integrated a 2.2-inch display into the top tube, and even provides a USB-C charging port for riders to be able to charge and connect devices. The Shimano Connect mobile app works with the new bicycle.
With all these fittings on, the bike is as light as you'd expect from a player in this segment, tipping the scales at 52 pounds (23.5 kg)
Honda didn't specifically say when the RN0 will hit the market, but I expect that to happen early next year. It's too early to tell how much the Japanese will charge for it, but to give you a taste of what to expect, I will tell you that the company refers to this vehicle using the word premium.
There will be three sizes on the table, S, M, and L, each of them individually engineered with size-specific dimensions. Only one color was announced for now for the frame, something called Pearl Moon Ash Gray, which matches the Ergon SM10 saddle.

FedEx Corp. has made clear that its future lies with premium B2B logistics services in key industrial verticals that require precision execution, such as automotive, healthcare, aerospace and data centers — not cheap last-mile delivery for online retailers. Add the defense sector to the list of industries the freight transportation giant is targeting for high- margin growth opportunities.
In August, FedEx Dataworks ( NYSE: FDX ) undertook a sweeping modernization of the U.S. Army’s domestic non-tactical logistics network, supply chain procedures and 23 government-owned and operated industrial facilities that make, repair, overhaul and store military equipment and munitions.
Dataworks is a division that uses analytics, artificial intelligence and digital technology to turn supply chain visibility into actionable intelligence. The real-time data platform harnesses huge amounts of operational signals gathered from millions of parcel and freight shipments to help businesses spot emerging risks early and coordinate responses before they can cause disruptions, optimize shipping routes, improve package tracking and provide supply chain insights. Its capabilities are designed to integrate with a customer’s existing tools and workflows. Dataworks recently began helping Stripe Capital explore how supply chain intelligence could open opportunities for small-and medium businesses to secure financing.
Management has repeatedly said it wants to leverage the company’s two petabytes of data and advanced AI capabilities to better support customers and drive new lines of revenue.
Last month, FedEx Dataworks announced on LinkedIn the hiring of retired Vice Admiral Dion English to be vice president and global lead – defense and government logistics solutions. During his Navy career he held leadership roles across global supply chain and logistics operations. Most recently, he led a multibillion-dollar global logistics enterprise spanning all combatant commands and more than 150 countries.
“This is just one example of our leadership role in logistics orchestration, which we view as a new market opportunity that complements our traditional shipping business. When it comes to physical AI, our network is already one of the most automated in the world,” CEO Raj Subramaniam said about the Army contract on Oct. 28 during the company’s quarterly earnings call.
FedEx has worked with the U.S. government for more than 30 years, including through its current work providing government-wide domestic and international small package delivery through the Next Generation Delivery Service contract. FedEx also provides cargo airlift to U.S. Transportation Command as a longstanding participant in the Civil Reserve Air Fleet.
To meet 21st century threats, the Army is overhauling its Cold War-era funding framework to partner directly with private capital markets and accelerate modernization through its new Strategic Capital Initiative. The project aims to match the Army’s most acute, strategic needs with investable, private sector commercial models to rapidly scale critical infrastructure upgrades — without waiting years for traditional procurement cycles to deliver critical capabilities to the frontline.
FedEx Dataworks logistics and technology experts are leading a team to integrate commercial predictive analytics and time-definite next-day delivery into Army depots with the goal of optimizing stock levels, demand forecasting and transportation routing to ensure soldiers receive parts, munitions and equipment ahead of operational demand, according to an article on the Army’s website.
Acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle tours facilities at Pine Bluff Arsenal in Arkansas Oct. 2029, 2026. The visit came as the Defense Department moves quickly to modernize the in-house industrial base. (Photo: U.S. Army/Staff Sgt. Amanda McLean)
“We are evaluating transportation routing and modes to cut delivery times across the Army, and transitioning from a dated supply system to a predictive, intelligent network to ensure the warfighter receives critical equipment at the time of need,” said Dave Fitzgerald, deputy undersecretary of the Army.
The Army and FedEx have formed working groups to analyze existing networks, processes and technologies, with a finalized implementation plan for U.S. based industrial sites expected this month.
Securing all the new logistics data is a top priority for the Army, which plans to host the new information system within Google’s highest level commercial cloud. The platform supports FedEx’s tools while integrating with the Army’s existing data systems, under identity management and encryption safeguards required for handling defense-related information.
Public private partnership
Marc Andersen, assistant secretary of the army for financial management and comptroller, also serves as chief investment officer for the Strategic Capital Initiative. He explained to investors and corporate executives in New York last Thursday that the service intends to revitalize industrial property by aligning venture capital and private equity with long-term government demand.
The immediate priority, he said, is for investments in digital computing infrastructure. Under the public-private model, private developers finance and build the facilities on Defense Department property at zero upfront taxpayer construction expense, operating a commercial side to generate steady revenue from these partnerships while providing the Army the potential to secure classified computing capability as in-kind value and surge support during national crises.
Under phase two of the Strategic Capital Initiative, commercial power developers are signing enhanced-use leases to build, own and operate microgrid-capable energy facilities on Army installations.
Andersen also highlighted new conditional lease awards designed to re-shore critical mineral supply chains, converting historical military depots into domestic processing hubs. Under the awards, the Army is establishing lithium processing at Red River Army Depot in Texas, synthetic and battery-grade graphite production at Anniston Army Depot in Alabama and Pine Bluff Arsenal in Arkansas, and processing for boron and heavy rare earth elements, including dysprosium and terbium, at Tooele Army Depot in Utah.
“The United States Army is open for business, and we’re moving out fast,” Andersen told investors.
Walmart supply chain meeting
Meanwhile, Acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle met Monday with leaders at Walmart’s headquarters in Bentonville, Arkansas, and visited the company’s Global Security Operations Center to share best practices on managing complex global supply chains through natural disasters and other disruptive global events. The discussion centered on how large-scale, globally dispersed enterprises maintain real-time situational awareness under those conditions to proactively anticipate disruptions, adapt on the fly and surge critical resources to teams in the field.

AstraZeneca has apparently made a $10 billion bid to acquire Rhythm Pharmaceuticals, an offer William Blair suspects will not be the last for the hot ticket metabolic biotech.
Rhythm Pharmaceuticals’ shares ended Wednesday up 24% on rumors that AstraZeneca had made a $10 billion bid to buy the biotech, which focuses on rare neuroendocrine diseases.
The Wall Street Journal reported the potential transaction , citing sources familiar with the matter. AstraZeneca reportedly offered $124 per share for Rhythm.
“We believe that this company would be a great strategic pickup for AstraZeneca,” William Blair wrote Wednesday afternoon. The firm had selected Rhythm as a likely takeout target earlier this year, with multiple potential buyers given its metabolic focus.
“We believe any large-cap biopharma company with a metabolic (diabetes, obesity, etc.) could be interested in this company,” the firm said. “In our view, that is basically every biopharma company out there.”
The star of the buyout would be injectable weight loss drug Imcivree, which won approval in March for its third FDA indication , this time for acquired hypothalamic obesity (aHO). William Blair anticipated that the drug could hit $3.6 billion in sales by 2032, not including the potential for an approval in Prader-Willi syndrome. Rhythm is planning a Phase 3 trial for that rare disease later this year, according to the firm.

Drilling at Controlled Thermal Resources’ Hell’s Kitchen geothermal energy and lithium project in southern California. Credit: Controlled Thermal Resources.
By: Andrew Seale November 5, 2026
Washington is backing California’s critical minerals push with loans, price guarantees and equity, but developers still face a hurdle federal support can’t remove: state environmental approval.
The state hosts the country’s only active commercial-scale rare earth mining and processing operation at MP Materials’ (NYSE: MP) Mountain Pass, while developers around the Salton Sea are trying to turn lithium-rich geothermal brines into battery materials. A rival project’s environmental review was sent back for revisions in August, two months after BHE Renewables and TerraLithium reported a technical breakthrough.
“California is a water-constrained state, and that makes it very difficult to approve projects like this,” Federico Gay, principal analyst for lithium at Benchmark Mineral Intelligence in London, told The Northern Miner in an October interview. “But the California Energy Commission and the government seem to be focused on supporting projects like this—more in words than in money, but potentially money will follow.”
The setback came on Aug. 11, when California’s Court of Appeal ruled that an Imperial County environmental review of privately held Controlled Thermal Resources’ Hell’s Kitchen project didn’t establish that its claimed 50-year water supply would be available or fully address air quality impacts. The county must address those gaps under the California Environmental Quality Act.
Midterms
Tuesday’s Democratic election victory adds uncertainty to federal support. The party’s capture of Congress raises the prospect of closer scrutiny of Washington’s mining investments and gives Democrats greater influence over negotiations to accelerate federal permitting.
Permitting mines in California requires navigating local land-use rules and state laws, including the California Environmental Quality Act and the Surface Mining and Reclamation Act. The latter requires reclamation plans, annual inspections and financial assurances for restoring mine sites.
Controlled Thermal Resources broke ground on its $1.85-billion (C$2.5-billion) Hell’s Kitchen project in Imperial Valley in 2024. The project, about 200 km east of San Diego, would use heat from geothermal brine to generate electricity and extract lithium before reinjecting the brine underground.
The company targets 50 megawatts of power by 2028 and annual lithium carbonate output of 25,000 tonnes by 2029, rising to 100,000 tonnes at full capacity. Controlled Thermal hasn’t said whether regulatory delays will change those timelines. It has signed supply agreements with General Motors (NYSE: GM) and Stellantis (NYSE: STLA).
The company announced an agreement in March with special purpose acquisition company Plum Acquisition Corp. IV (Nasdaq: PLMK). The merger is expected to close in the fourth quarter, with Controlled Thermal listing on Nasdaq under the symbol CTRH.
Warren Buffett
BHE Renewables, controlled by the Warren Buffett-formed Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE: BRK.A, BRK.B), operates 10 geothermal power plants in Imperial Valley. It plans to add lithium extraction to its existing infrastructure through a joint venture formed in 2024 with TerraLithium, a unit of Occidental Petroleum (NYSE: OXY).
The partners announced in June that they had produced lithium chloride from geothermal brine at BHE’s Calipatria plant and then manufactured battery-grade lithium carbonate.
The tests are a step towards commercial production, though BHE hasn’t announced a start date. Recovering lithium from its existing geothermal plants could yield about 90,000 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent annually, the company estimates. It hasn’t provided a water-use estimate.
“Capital requirements are quite high, and the processing side of things has several technological and technical difficulties that make it very difficult,” Gay said. “But the potential is massive.”
A 2023 Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory study estimated 4.1 million tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent in the well-characterized portion of the Salton Sea geothermal reservoir, rising to 18 million tonnes across its probable extent.
Hell’s Kitchen could reach commercial production in the early 2030s, followed by BHE in the mid-2030s, Gay said.
Federal backing
In the Mojave Desert, Washington is acting as customer, lender and investor in MP Materials’ Mountain Pass operation.
Under a July 2025 agreement , the U.S. Department of Defense established a 10-year price floor of $110 per kg for MP’s neodymium-praseodymium products. A separate 10-year agreement covers purchases of magnets from MP’s planned 10X plant.
The department bought $400 million of convertible preferred stock and a warrant that, if converted and exercised, would give it about 15% of MP’s common shares and make it the company’s largest shareholder. It also provided a $150-million loan to expand heavy rare earth separation.
MP produced 840 tonnes of neodymium-praseodymium in the second quarter, 41% more than a year earlier despite an extended planned shutdown in April. Sales exceeded 1,000 tonnes for a second consecutive quarter, the company said in its quarterly results .
The company reached mechanical completion of its first heavy rare earth separation circuit at Mountain Pass in May. Its dysprosium-terbium circuit, designed to produce 200 tonnes annually of the two heavy rare earths used in high-performance magnets, is being commissioned.
MP’s Independence campus in Fort Worth, Texas, manufactures magnets. The company began shipping magnets to General Motors for qualification in the second quarter, with commercial shipments targeted by year-end, executives said on its earnings call.
Gold projects
In the eastern Mojave, Equinox Gold (TSX, NYSE-A: EQX) is advancing stage two of its Castle Mountain mine, the Bureau of Land Management’s first mining project to receive full coverage under FAST-41.
A 2021 feasibility study projected average production of 218,000 oz. gold annually over 14 years, followed by residual heap leaching. Stage one heap leaching operated from November 2020 to August 2024.
FAST-41 coordinates environmental reviews and permitting timetables. The federal dashboard estimates completion of Castle Mountain’s environmental review and permitting by April 30, 2027.
“We’re in the final stages of permitting at the federal level,” Etienne Morin, Equinox’s chief capital markets officer, told The Northern Miner.
Equinox’s South Railroad project across the border in Nevada completed its federal environmental review and permitting under FAST-41 in August.
“It’s been very helpful for South Railroad, and we’re hoping that it’s going to be the same thing for Castle,” Morin said.
State permits are also required for stage two, though they will be extensions of existing operating permits, he said.
Equinox is continuing to extend the life of its Mesquite gold mine, 320 km south of Castle Mountain. The mine is expected to produce 70,000 to 80,000 oz. this year.
“It’s the gift that keeps on giving,” Morin said. “We keep finding more and extending the mine life.”
Mesquite, in Imperial County, has produced more than 5 million oz. since operations began in 1986.
“We’d like to be able to continue drilling, but that would probably require some infrastructure displacement,” Morin said. “We’re taking our time to make sure that we have all the stakeholders involved in those decisions.”
Fremont restart
In the Sierra Nevada foothills, Lode Gold Resources (TSXV: LOD; US-OTC: LODFF) is working to restart the former Fremont mine in Mariposa County. The county approved a three-year administrative use permit on Aug. 10 for surface drilling on the company’s private patented land. A 3,500- to 4,500-metre drilling program is under way.
“We’re reconfirming a lot of the historical workings and doing some small step-out drilling,” Kevin Shum, Lode’s head of investor relations, told The Northern Miner.
Fremont produced 125,000 oz. gold at 10.7 grams per tonne between 1849 and 1942. A May 2026 resource update outlined 18.8 million indicated tonnes grading 1.84 grams gold per tonne for 1.11 million oz., plus 33.1 million inferred tonnes at 1.86 grams for 1.98 million ounces.
Operations stopped during the Second World War.
“We’re working very closely with the community down in Fremont to get the permit reissued and updated,” Shum said.
The prospect of local jobs has attracted community support, he said. But, as California’s lithium developers have found, interest doesn’t guarantee approval.
“There’s always a challenge in the state of California.”

With backing from three Big Pharma investment arms, British biotech T-Therapeutics is brewing up a clinical launch for its cancer and autoimmune T cell engagers.
T-Therapeutics has bagged $133 million in series B funding to move its next-gen T cell engager therapeutics into the clinic for cancer and autoimmune diseases .
The oversubscribed series B was co-led by new investors Advent Life Sciences and British Business Bank, with participation from a slew of Big Pharma backers, including Johnson & Johnson Innovation, Eli Lilly and Sanofi Ventures, among other investors.
The U.K. biotech will use the new cash infusion to speed its T cell receptor (TCR) bispecific lead programs into the clinic. The cancer asset, dubbed TTX-008, targets CD3 for solid tumors, while the immunology candidate, called TTX-018, targets the same protein complex but for autoimmune and inflammation disorders.
Both programs stem from T-Therapeutics’ OpTiMus platform, which provides fully human TCRs to tackle historically difficult-to-reach intracellular targets. Initially formed in 2022, the biotech raised a total of $91 million in series A money after closing an extension in November 2025.
“This financing is a key step in our transition to a clinical-stage company, enabling us to accelerate the development of two oncology and immunology programs with pan-indication, blockbuster potential, underpinned by a platform that reaches targets long considered undruggable,” T-Therapeutics CEO Theodora Harold said in a Thursday release.
At the same time, the U.K. startup is also welcoming Kirsty Crame aboard as chief development officer. Crame previously served as Swiss pharma Curatis’ chief medical officer, with experience at Medigene and Gadeta before that.

A.P. Moller-Maersk raised its full-year earnings forecast on Thursday after higher freight rates drove a sharp increase in third-quarter profit, but its shares fell as the results and upgraded outlook disappointed investors. The stock dropped as much as 11.6% in Copenhagen trading.
The Danish shipping and logistics group (OTC: AMKBY ) reported quarterly earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, or EBITDA, of $4.7 billion, up from $2.7 billion a year earlier. That fell short of the $5.04 billion average forecast in an LSEG analyst poll, despite a 27% increase in revenue to $18.1 billion.
Maersk, the world’s second-largest container liner, now expects full-year underlying EBITDA of $14 billion to $14.5 billion, compared with its previous forecast of $10.5 billion to $12.5 billion. It also raised its underlying earnings before interest and taxes, or EBIT, forecast to $8 billion to $8.5 billion from $4.5 billion to $6.5 billion. Free cash flow is expected to exceed $3 billion, versus its previous forecast of above zero.
The increase marks Maersk’s third profit-guidance upgrade this year. The company attributed the latest revision to its third-quarter performance and improved visibility for the remainder of 2026, with the outlook based on global container-market volume growth of around 4%.
Analysts cited by Dow Jones said expectations had risen following strong outlook revisions from rivals Hapag-Lloyd and Zim.
Maersk partners with Hapag-Lloyd in Gemini ocean services.
Maersk’s Ocean division generated quarterly operating profit of about $2.6 billion, up from $567 million a year earlier, as higher freight rates more than offset a slight decline in cargo volumes. The result nevertheless missed a FactSet forecast of $3.07 billion.
Maersk benefited more from what it charged to transport containers than from carrying additional cargo. Volumes in its main shipping business fell about 1%, even as global container demand increased between 2% and 4% during the quarter.
At group level, EBIT increased to $3.3 billion from $1.3 billion, producing an operating margin of 18.1%. Growth extended beyond ocean shipping as Logistics & Services revenue rose 13%, with its EBIT margin improving to 5.8%, while Terminals reported record revenue and maintained strong earnings.
Elevated freight rates have benefited from port congestion and resilient demand. Those conditions helped Maersk raise its earnings expectations substantially even without strong growth in its own shipping volumes.
The company said its financial performance remains subject to uncertainty around macroeconomic conditions, bunker-fuel prices and freight rates. It also continued executing its $1 billion share-buyback program.
Why it matters: Elevated freight rates helped Maersk raise earnings expectations even without strong growth in volumes.

Segway came to EICMA this year with a surprisingly broad lineup of new electric motorcycles, ranging from high-performance concepts to off-road machines. But perhaps the most interesting of the bunch is also the one that looks the least like a conventional motorcycle or scooter.
Meet the Segway X Cruiser , an electric two-wheeler that takes motorcycle safety so seriously that it has a roll cage and seatbelts.
Or at least, those are among the configurations Segway is showing as it develops the new machine for production.
The X Cruiser is Segway’s attempt to bring more automotive-style protection to a single-track vehicle, essentially asking how much of a car’s safety envelope can be wrapped around a motorcycle without adding another pair of wheels.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
From the looks of things, the answer is quite a lot.
Segway says the X Cruiser’s design was informed by automotive crash scenarios, with cage and semi-cage structures, four-direction collision protection, staged energy absorption, and seatbelt restraints intended to improve rider protection. It also gets active safety features including standard blind spot detection and lane change warning.
The company showed several ways that basic idea can be configured, ranging from a more conventional partially enclosed scooter-like setup to versions with significantly more structure surrounding the rider. One of the most striking configurations uses a heavily bolstered race-car-style seat and seatbelt along with protective framing around the rider, while another adds a roof for even more enclosure.
It’s a fascinating approach because motorcycles have traditionally relied largely on the rider wearing the protection. Helmets, jackets, gloves, boots and sometimes airbag vests form the safety system, while the motorcycle itself generally offers little physical protection during a crash.
The X Cruiser effectively flips part of that equation by building some of the protective structure into the vehicle itself.
There’s an important caveat here, though. Segway specifically notes that its descriptions refer to the vehicle’s current design and equipment and do not mean it has completed automotive-style crash certification. Final equipment and certification will depend on individual markets, so it sounds like the company is holding short of making any major certification claims. Still though, it’s easy to see how having what is effectively a racing seat and roll cage surrounding the rider could seriously contribute to better protection in a crash. Just remember to keep your hands and feet within the vehicle at all times.
And unlike plenty of wild EICMA showpieces, this one isn’t merely destined to live under convention-center spotlights. Segway says the X Cruiser has a confirmed mass-production plan, with launches planned for China and Europe between 2027 and 2028. There’s no US availability announcement yet.
Underneath all that protective hardware is a fairly serious electric touring platform. Segway is using its CTB (cell-to-body) battery integration to help improve structural rigidity and battery packaging, with the company targeting nearly 200 km (124 miles) of range.
European versions are expected to feature 4.5 kW Type 2 AC charging, while the Chinese version will offer optional higher-power DC fast charging. The bike rolls on 15-inch front and 14-inch rear wheels wearing Michelin City Grip tires, and riders get a 10.25-inch TFT display along with an optional 55-liter electrically operated top box.
Interestingly, the X Cruiser also incorporates certain two-wheeler intellectual property and know-how licensed from BMW Group, though Segway stresses that it is responsible for the vehicle’s development, integration, validation, production and certification.
Segway had plenty more electric motorcycles at EICMA
The X Cruiser may be the weirdest – and thus perhaps the most interesting – of Segway’s EICMA debuts, but it was far from alone.
The company also unveiled the Segway Orca Concept, a futuristic high-performance electric maxi-scooter concept built around an 800V electrical architecture and a nearly 20 kWh battery.
Segway is targeting up to 300 km (186 miles) of range, a 0-100 km/h (0-62 mph) time of 4.5 seconds, and the ability to add 200 km (124 miles) of range in 20 minutes. The concept also features front and rear multi-link suspension, electronically controlled multi-mode damping and a battery-integrated CTB chassis. Those figures are engineering targets rather than promised production specifications, and Segway currently describes the Orca strictly as a concept.
Then there’s Segway’s expanding X Series , which moves the focus away from urban riding and toward dirt. The lineup includes the Xaber X1000 and Xaber 350, along with different Xaber 300 variants for the US and European markets. Segway is also partnering with Michelin for its Dakar Rally Factory Team, using the brutal rally environment as a real-world development and validation platform for electric off-road motorcycles.
Taken together, it’s quite the showing from a company whose name many people still associate primarily with those funny two-wheeled self-balancing machines from the early 2000s.
Segway has already expanded heavily into electric scooters, e-bikes, go-karts and powersports vehicles. Now it seems increasingly serious about becoming an electric motorcycle company as well.
And if motorcycles with roll cages, roofs and seatbelts are part of that future, things could get pretty interesting… pretty quickly!

John Deere plans to close its Ottumwa, Iowa, factory and end manufacturing at its Hagie plant in Clarion, Iowa, as it moves equipment production among existing factories in the United States and Brazil.
What’s Related
The changes will unfold over Deere’s fiscal years 2027 through 2029. Windrower and round baler production will move from Ottumwa to Deere’s Des Moines Works in Ankeny, Iowa, while Hagie STS sprayer production will move from Clarion to Thibodaux, Louisiana.
Deere also plans to move sugar cane harvester production from Thibodaux to Catalão, Brazil, and small planter production from Moline, Illinois, to Paton, Iowa. The company cited changing customer demand and available factory space as reasons for moving production to Iowa.
Deere told DTN that more than 300 people work at Ottumwa and more than 200 work at Clarion. The company has not announced a final number of job cuts.
RELATED: John Deere Squashes Shutdown Rumors With $20 Billion U.S. Investment
What's going where
Windrower production will move to Des Moines Works by the end of fiscal 2027, followed by round balers by the end of fiscal 2028. Deere intends to close the Ottumwa factory once those transfers are complete.
Deere will begin moving Hagie STS sprayers to Louisiana in fiscal 2028, with manufacturing at Clarion ending by fiscal 2029. Small planter production will move small planter production to Paton in fiscal 2027.
Sugar cane harvester production will shift to Brazil in fiscal 2029. Deere already makes the machines in Catalão and said the move will bring production closer to its largest concentration of customers in South America.
The Louisiana factory currently produces about 35 sugar cane harvesters annually for the U.S. market. Deere told DTN it does not expect the change to reduce headcount at Thibodaux because sprayer production will move there.
More sourcing changes may be coming. Deere’s Construction and Forestry division is also reviewing how it sources parts and production work to manage costs and respond to changing demand. The announcement does not identify specific changes.
Employment impact remains uncertain
Deere spokesperson Dustin Lemmon told the Iowa Capital Dispatch that about 300 people would be affected at normal production levels, but the actual employment impact remains uncertain. Ottumwa city officials put the number higher, telling WQAD the closure will cost about 400 jobs and more than $30 million in payroll. Possible employee assistance includes transfers, retraining, relocation assistance, and severance benefits.
Deere is “currently operating far below normal production volumes due to the downturn in the ag economy ,” Lemmon said.
The company said it will work with employees, union representatives where applicable, and local leaders during the transitions. It also plans to identify future uses for the Ottumwa and Clarion sites.
Deere said in its announcement that it expects to keep serving customers without disruption during the moves and that it aims to maintain product quality, availability and service.

World’s First: AutoFlight Nails a 5-eVTOL Autonomous Formation Flight in China
9 photos
Photo: AutoFlight
AutoFlight isn’t just another eVTOL (electric vertical takeoff and landing) maker. It has developed a 2-ton eVTOL that comes in two configurations (the cargo CarryAll, and the firefighting CarryAll), as well as a 5-ton eVTOL (the Matrix), and all of these flew together recently in what is claimed to be the world’s first 5-eVTOL formation flight.
On October 31 and November 1, a few alumni representatives from the Stanford Executive Program (SEP) at Stanford Graduate School of Business were among the lucky guests who had the opportunity to watch a global premiere related to eVTOL technology. Five eVTOL in two different weight classes flew together seamlessly, without any pilot onboard.
One was a 5-ton V5000 Matrix, and the other four were in the 2-ton class, across two different models (the V2000CG CarryAll cargo and the V2000CGF CarryAll firefighting). These five AutoFlight aircraft completed a coordinated, fully autonomous flight for 47 minutes, with the V5000 Matrix (which acted as the lead) covering more than 1433 km (82.6 miles).
This extraordinary demonstration took place in Kunshan, China, where AutoFlight operates its Bailian Lake Flight Test Base. Apart from the Stanford alumni representatives, AutoFlight customers and players in the international eVTOL industry were also invited to attend. And there was even more excitement when all of them got to watch the formation flight in the most unique way, while onboard AutoFlight’s futuristic floating vertiport, the Sunship.
The Chinese AAM company has been working its way to this global premiere. Earlier this year, it completed a three-aircraft formation demonstration. That flight was carried out by one 5-ton Matrix and two 2-ton Prosperity eVTOLs. Building on the success of that May demonstration , this recent formation flight took things to the next level, especially considering the challenging wind conditions on the second day.
The point of all this is to take steps toward autonomous multi-aircraft operations in the future, and building transport networks that could connect long-haul, regional, and last-mile routes. It’s a much more complex vision of AAM (Advanced Air Mobility) than basic air taxi service and cargo. The ability to successfully coordinate eVTOL of different sizes and with different roles, all flying without a pilot, requires incredible planning and safety management.
Just as impressive as the aircraft themselves is AutoFlight’s Sunship, one of the most futuristic vertiport concepts. Defined as a water-based green vertiport, this floating platform runs on electric power, with solar power for range extension, and supports fast eVTOL charging.
It was developed for high efficiency across five applications, from urban commuting, sea-air tourism, and emergency response, to the industry of offshore energy, and mobile airports (multiple Sunships connected together to form a distributed vertiport system).
AutoFlight’s Prosperity eVTOL for passenger transportation is on its way to full certification, while the cargo CarryAll version is already the first in its category (2-ton class) to be fully certified.
