Battery-electric cars took 32% of the UK’s new car market in October, while petrol cars fell to just 37.2%, according to new data from the SMMT. That’s the closest the two have been.
At the current pace, electric cars will outsell petrol in the UK within a year. And it could happen as soon as this December.
October: EVs up 33%, petrol down 12%
The UK registered 152,730 new cars in October, up 5.4% year-over-year and the 11th straight month of growth for the overall market.
All of that growth came from plug-ins. BEV registrations jumped 32.7% to 48,858 units, and plug-in hybrids rose 30.1% to 22,898. Meanwhile, petrol fell 11.6% to 56,876 units, diesel dropped 15.9%, and even conventional hybrids were down 5%.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Through the first 10 months of the year, the UK has now registered 503,805 BEVs, up 30.4%, for a 26.6% market share. Petrol’s year-to-date share is down to 41.1%, from 47.2% at the same point last year.
The trend points to 2027, or sooner
We pulled SMMT’s monthly fuel-type data going back to March 2024 to see where this is heading. Note that SMMT counts mild hybrids as petrol (or diesel) in its headline categories, and that’s generally how we count them at Electrek.
Monthly UK market share of battery-electric and petrol cars since March 2024, with linear trends extended. Source: SMMT, chart: Electrek
In March 2024, petrol held 55.9% of the market and BEVs 15.2%. In October 2026, it was 37.2% vs 32.0%. Petrol’s share is shrinking by about half a point per month on a linear trend, while BEVs gain about 0.36 points a month. Extend both lines and they cross around August 2027 at roughly 33% each.
But that’s the slow scenario, because it ignores December.
UK BEV share spikes every December as automakers push volume to get closer to their ZEV Mandate targets. BEVs hit 31.0% in December 2024 and 32.2% in December 2025, when petrol was at 39.4%. Over the last five months, BEV share has run about 5 points higher than a year earlier, and petrol about 7 points lower. If December follows that pattern, BEVs land around 37% and petrol around 32%.
That would be the first time BEVs beat petrol in SMMT’s headline numbers, mild hybrids included.
However, SMMT’s own forecast of 27.2% BEV share for the full year implies roughly 31% for November and December combined, which would make it a much closer call. And on a stricter definition that puts mild hybrids with hybrids instead of petrol, BEVs already outsold every other powertrain in August .
Zoom out to full years and the picture is just as clear. Cars that run only on petrol or diesel, mild hybrids included, made up 72.5% of the UK market in 2021. This year, they’re at 45.5%.
Full-year UK market share of combustion cars (petrol and diesel, including mild hybrids) vs battery-electric cars. 2026 is year-to-date through October. Source: SMMT, chart: Electrek
Automakers still want the mandate cut
None of this is good enough for the SMMT, which is using the release to push the government, again, to cut the ZEV Mandate targets.
The mandate requires 33% of 2026 sales to be zero-emission. SMMT now forecasts 27.2%. It expects 32% next year against a 38% target, and 37.5% in 2028 against 52%, a 14.5-point gap.
UK BEV share vs. ZEV Mandate targets. 2026-2028 figures are from SMMT’s November 2026 market outlook. Source: SMMT, chart: Electrek
The trade group says automakers have spent “billions” on discounts, 0% financing, deposit contributions, and even subsidized charging to move EVs, on top of the government’s Electric Car Grant. It also slammed last week’s Budget, which confirmed a new EV-specific road tax (eVED) starting in 2028 and kept 20% VAT on public charging.
“Higher targets may force supply, but they do not create demand,” SMMT chief executive Mike Hawes said.
We’ve heard this one before. The SMMT made the same argument after September’s record 99,199 BEV registrations , and the government already opened a review of the mandate this year.
Chinese brands are taking the growth
This might be the main reason why the trade group wants to slow things down. The brands growing fastest in the UK are mostly Chinese. BYD registered 6,065 cars in October, up 73%. Jaecoo more than doubled to 6,089 units, Chery nearly tripled to 3,707, and Leapmotor doubled to 1,773. MG was up 85%.
Tesla, on the other hand, registered just 282 cars in October, down 45% from 511 a year ago. The first month of the quarter is always slow for Tesla in the UK, and the brand is still up 31% year-to-date at 46,526 units after a big September. But it didn’t have a single model in October’s top 10 BEVs, which was led by the Skoda Enyaq (1,568), Mini Countryman (1,494), and Jaecoo 5 (1,465).
Electrek’s Take
The SMMT’s framing is that there’s a “demand gap.” The data shows the opposite. BEV registrations are up 30% this year while petrol is shrinking every single month. That’s not a market rejecting EVs.
Top comment by European Bob
Liked by 5 people
The SMMT is not a neutral organisation, they have been briefing against EVs for years and continue to do so.
The ZEV mandate is NOT a measure of how many pure BEVs are sold, and the SMMT know it, it's a measure of REDUCING emission against a level set in the past.
Those emissions reductions can be met by selling BEVs, or selling more efficient PHEVs or even selling more efficient petrol or diesel cars! The manufacturers can also buy credits if they choose to.
NO manufacturer has paid any ZEV fines to date (DfT announcement March 2026)
As for the "heavy discounts" and "loss making sales", well I have two data points on that.
1. The retail price of EVs has continued to climb in the UK over the past 6 years, despite the cost of any average 50kWh battery pack dropping several thousand dollars.
2. There are hundreds of main dealerships who are buying cars from the manufacturers, driving them for the minimum 3 month period, often with just a few thousand miles on the clock and then selling them with a 30-35% retail price discount, and then repeating ad infinitum. The dealerships are still making a few thousand with each transaction, so we know where the manufacturers price really sits.
View all comments
And the discounts automakers keep complaining about? That’s the mandate doing exactly what it was designed to do. It forces automakers to sell EVs, so they price them to sell, and buyers respond. Hawes says targets don’t create demand, but cheaper EVs clearly do. October proves it.
Now, is the jump to 52% in 2028 steep? It is steep, but it looks achievable to me. If anything is hurting demand, it’s the government’s own moves: a new EV-only road tax and 20% VAT on public charging. That’s what the industry should be fighting. It’s too early for that.
Either way, petrol’s days as the UK’s default car are numbered. The only question is whether the milestone comes in December or sometime in 2027. Our bet is December.

A potential strike by port watchmen at Los Angeles and Long Beach has been delayed again after the Pacific Maritime Association and International Longshore and Warehouse Union Local 26 agreed to extend their contract through midnight Pacific Time on Friday.
Negotiations will continue Friday with assistance from federal mediators.
The latest extension follows an earlier agreement that pushed a potential walkout from Nov. 1 to 5 p.m. Pacific on Wednesday.
“The Pacific Maritime Association and ILWU Local 26 have agreed to extend their contract through midnight Pacific Time on Friday night, November 6,” the PMA said in a statement. “Negotiations will continue on Friday with the help of the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service. Local 26 represents about 250 watchmen, roughly 2% of the ILWU workforce at the ports. PMA remains committed to reaching a fair agreement at the bargaining table that avoids disruption at the nation’s two busiest ports.”
The dispute involves 250 watchmen who perform security-related duties at marine terminals. A walkout would potentially affect terminals that handle more than half of the ports’ cargo, including roughly 85% at Long Beach and 33% at Los Angeles.
A strike could have consequences beyond security operations. PMA has warned that other ILWU members, including longshore workers and marine clerks covered by separate contracts, are expected to honor Local 26 picket lines. That could interrupt vessel loading and unloading, container-yard activity and truck-gate operations at affected terminals.
The watchmen’s previous agreement expired in July 2025, and employees have continued working under extensions while the union and employers negotiate a replacement. Local 26 members authorized a strike after more than a year of bargaining.
These talks are separate from the broader West Coast longshore agreement covering approximately 22,000 workers at 29 ports, which remains in effect through 2028.
Why it matters: The extension buys time to avoid a potentially major supply-chain disruption at the busiest U.S. container port complex.

The U.S. Capitol in Washington. Democratic control could bring closer examination of federal mining investments. Credit: DAVID ILIFF/Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0.
Posted By: Colin McClelland November 5, 2026
Democrats’ capture of Congress could put U.S. mining investments under closer scrutiny and sustain demand for gold as political stalemate complicates business planning, according to analysts and policy specialists.
Federal support for projects could face tougher examination without necessarily slowing environmental approvals, while uncertainty over trade and economic policy could encourage investors to buy precious metals, CPM Group managing partner Jeffrey Christian and Aaron Mintzes, deputy policy director and counsel at environmental group Earthworks, told The Northern Miner .
“We expect inflation to remain high and problematic, and do not expect any reductions in government spending to reduce inflationary pressures,” Christian said in emailed answers. “The inflationary pressures are coming from a much broader array of developments.”
The comments sharpen the distinction between scrutiny of Washington’s financial backing for mining companies and changes to the rules governing project development. Democrats’ victory gives them greater influence over spending and oversight, but leaves President Donald Trump with executive powers and a veto over legislation. For developers, the question is whether federal support will remain dependable as lawmakers examine how recipients were chosen.
Markets surge
Mining shares outpaced a broad stock market rally on Wednesday following the election. The S&P/TSX Global Mining Index gained 5.1%, while the S&P/TSX Global Gold Index surged 8.7% as bullion rebounded.
Canada’s S&P/TSX Composite advanced 2.3% and the junior-heavy S&P/TSX Venture Composite added 2.5%. In New York, the Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 3%, or 1,569 points, while the S&P 500 gained 1.6% and the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.4%.
The election has already triggered a rotation across commodities as investors weigh slower U.S. data centre construction and a possible easing of Middle East tensions, BMO Capital Markets said Thursday in a note.
Gold rebounded above $4,100 per oz. as the dollar and Treasury yields fell, accompanied by sharp gains in silver and platinum group metals. Copper and tin, which are exposed to artificial intelligence infrastructure spending, underperformed, while zinc, nickel and aluminum proved more resilient, the bank said.
Crude oil fell below $95 a barrel for the first time since the summer, from more than $110 a week earlier, BMO said.
Funding focus
Government investments in mining companies are likely to become an oversight priority, Mintzes said. But he questioned whether Democratic control would itself delay projects.
“Slowing projects, probably not,” he said in emailed answers. “After all, Congress is debating the permitting legislation that prevents slowing projects.”
Senator Martin Heinrich and Representative Jared Huffman, the senior Democrats on the Senate energy and House natural resources committees, sought a watchdog investigation in August into government investments in private mining companies.
Their request asked the Government Accountability Office to examine financial safeguards and potential conflicts when federal agencies act as both investors and regulators. It also questioned how agencies assess project economics before committing taxpayer funds.
Christian argued that greater scrutiny could delay financing for projects whose economics do not justify federal support. He did not identify individual projects or provide supporting economic assessments in his response.
Permitting divide
Mintzes sees room for a permitting agreement when the new Congress takes office, but favours retaining electricity transmission measures while changing the mining provisions.
Both parties face pressure from Indigenous groups and communities to oppose the existing Senate package, he said. Earthworks has criticized the bill’s proposed restrictions on legal challenges and changes to environmental safeguards.
The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act would strengthen review deadlines, restrict agencies’ ability to revoke permits and narrow the window for litigation. Republican senators Shelley Moore Capito and Mike Lee joined Democrats Sheldon Whitehouse and Heinrich in sponsoring the proposed legislation before the election.
Huffman argued before the election that Democrats should seek a better agreement once they had greater negotiating power. His objections included protections for communities and wildlife, as well as assurances that renewable energy projects would receive fair treatment.
“Folding our hand now or in the lame duck makes no sense,” he said in a September statement outlining his objections.
Wood Mackenzie offered a more optimistic assessment after the election, identifying permitting reform as the likeliest area for bipartisan agreement because both parties face pressure to lower electricity costs.
The Senate has scheduled a procedural vote for Nov. 9 on advancing the legislation serving as the vehicle for the permitting package.
Gold protection
For precious metals, Christian sees political stalemate adding to existing economic and geopolitical risks rather than resolving them.
Those pressures are likely to stimulate renewed investor buying of gold and silver, he said. CPM sees the metals’ recent price declines as at or near a bottom.
His assessment does not depend on the weaker dollar and falling interest rates that helped explain gold’s initial post-election rally.
“We do not see a weaker dollar in the near term,” Christian said. “We expect interest rates to remain ‘high’ and possibly increase until recessionary conditions are more clearly emerging.”
BMO also cautioned against assuming an immediate change in the economic outlook. The election had not prompted changes to its baseline growth, inflation or interest-rate forecasts, chief U.S. economist Scott Anderson said during a webcast from London on Wednesday.
Democrats would have limited ability to reverse existing legislation without presidential cooperation, he said.
Data centre risks
Christian sees a more direct demand risk for copper and silver if increased scrutiny slows data centre construction. Regulation would be only one constraint.
“Financing also will be a constraint to future data center developments, as will energy availability, water, and an absence of local buy-in,” he said.
Physical shortages are cushioning copper against those demand concerns. Chinese smelters are moderating production as processing margins turn negative, tightening an already constrained spot market, BMO said Thursday, citing CRU estimates. The Shanghai futures market is showing its steepest backwardation since 2022, with nearby metal commanding a premium over later delivery.
Christian expects continued conflict between the administration and Congress over trade policy, making investment decisions harder even where demand remains strong.
“Trade conditions will flip back and forth as a result, reducing business’s ability to plan effectively,” he said.

Gold treasures, including the grand prize, are waiting to be found. Credit: Adobe Stock
By: Northern Miner Staff November 5, 2026
Read the French version: https://www.northernminer.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/French-version.pdf
More than 80,000 Canadians have joined the adventure, discovering the remarkable stories of the mining industry that helped build our nation. Now, with 241 oz. of gold still hidden across the country, the hunt is far from over.
Somewhere in Canada, a treasure chest containing 217 1-oz. gold coins is waiting to be discovered.
Four more treasures, each containing 6 oz. of pure gold, are hidden in Quebec, Saskatchewan, Manitoba and the Sudbury region of Ontario.
That’s 241 oz. of gold still waiting to be found . And somewhere out there, someone has the chance to turn a little curiosity, a love of adventure and some Canadian ingenuity into a life-changing discovery.
But as The Northern Miner ‘s Great Canadian Treasure Hunt celebrates its first year, it’s clear that something bigger than gold has been uncovered.
Across the country, Canadians have been rediscovering the stories, characters and achievements of the mining industry that helped build the country.
And they’re having fun doing it.
Treasure hunt nation
When The Northern Miner launched the Great Canadian Treasure Hunt in August last year, the idea was simple: What if we could get Canadians excited about mining by turning our country’s remarkable mining history into a real-life treasure hunt?
Participants could explore that history and have the chance to make a gold discovery of their own.
The response has exceeded our expectations.
More than 80,500 Canadians have become active treasure hunters , following clues, studying maps, watching videos and learning about communities and discoveries they may never have heard of before.
The Hunt has connected with millions across its website and social media platforms, while hundreds of news reports, television appearances and radio interviews have carried the excitement into communities from coast to coast.
Perhaps the most rewarding part has been seeing Canadians connect with the adventure — and with one another.
There were brothers Jason and Matthew Schwarz, separated by 4,000 km, who spent months working together to solve clues before discovering 6 oz. of gold in British Columbia’s legendary Golden Triangle.
For the brothers, the real treasure may have been the time spent reconnecting.
Then there were young geology graduates Oliver Baker and Bella Ruppert, who tracked down a treasure near Bathurst, N.B., only to nearly walk away because they weren’t convinced the disguised box was what they were looking for.
Fortunately, curiosity got the better of them. They returned, checked again and struck gold.
These are the stories that have made the Hunt special: Canadians embracing adventure, exploring their country and occasionally walking away considerably richer.
Mining’s next generation
Of course, the Great Canadian Treasure Hunt has always been about more than gold.
Canada is one of the world’s great mining nations. From the gold rushes that opened the West to the nickel discoveries that helped industrialize the country, mining has created communities, supported generations of families and helped build the prosperity Canadians enjoy today.
And its importance is only growing.
Speaking at Canada House in London in October, energy and natural resources Minister Tim Hodgson, declared that the world is entering the “largest investment supercycle in the history of the metals and mining industry.”
He explained that critical minerals are no longer simply industrial commodities, but essential ingredients that will determine which countries can grow, compete and secure their economic futures.
It’s a powerful reminder that the minerals beneath Canadian soil aren’t just part of our history. They’re central to our future.
Copper that carries electricity, nickel used in advanced technologies, uranium that fuels nuclear reactors and potash that helps feed the world are all part of Canada’s mineral wealth.
And that’s a story worth sharing with young Canadians who may never have considered a career in mining.
The early signs are encouraging.
Seventeen per cent of the Hunt’s social media audience is 24 or younger, far above the proportion traditionally following mining news.
Over the past year, MINING.com Jobs has recorded more than one million job views, an increase of 283%, while applications have risen 23%. Although those gains cannot be attributed solely to the Hunt, they are encouraging signs of growing interest in mining careers.
The adventure has also inspired the Junior Explorers Challenge, developed with Mining Matters, giving children aged nine to 17 an opportunity to explore Canada’s geology and mining history through puzzles, quizzes and creative challenges.
Today’s curious young treasure hunter could become tomorrow’s geologist, engineer or mining entrepreneur.
That would give the adventure a lasting impact.
Five treasures remain
As we prepare for another year of treasure hunting, there’s unfinished business.
The grand prize remains unclaimed, along with four regional treasures, each containing six one-ounce gold coins.
Remember, these aren’t just fascinating stories about Canada’s mining past. Hidden within each original article and its accompanying video are clues that could help you find real gold.
Here’s a look at the histories behind the four regional hunts that remain active.
Quebec: Gold, grit, the road north
Nested deep in northwestern Quebec lies one of Canada’s greatest gold-producing regions, where determination, ambition and a little prospecting luck transformed wilderness into thriving communities.
Exploring our Quebec treasure story takes us to Val-d’Or, whose name means valley of gold .
20th-century hardships during the Great Depression, when jobs were scarce, drove prospectors into the forests of the Abitibi region searching for opportunity.
60 miles from the Ontario border, among them was Jean-Jacques “Jack” Sullivan, whose discoveries helped ignite a gold rush that transformed the region.
5 major mines—including Sullivan, Lamaque and Sigma—helped turn a remote settlement into a thriving mining city. Roads, railways, schools and businesses followed.
Mining discoveries didn’t just produce gold. They created livelihoods, built communities and helped establish Quebec as one of the world’s great mining jurisdictions. Today, the Abitibi region remains an important centre of Canadian gold production and exploration, proof that a great mining district can deliver opportunity for generations. And somewhere in Quebec, six one-ounce gold coins await a treasure hunter who can unlock the clues hidden in this history.
Ready to hunt for Quebec’s hidden gold? Explore the original story and watch the embedded video for clues that could lead you to the treasure.
Read the Quebec treasure story: Gold, Grit and the Road to the North
Saskatchewan’s buried treasure
Not every great Canadian treasure glitters.
Some of the most valuable minerals ever discovered in this country are pink.
Beneath Saskatchewan’s seemingly endless wheat fields lie some of the world’s richest potash deposits, essential to producing the fertilizer that helps farmers feed billions of people.
Their origins stretch back more than 350 million years, when an ancient inland sea covered much of what is now Saskatchewan.
As the sea evaporated, it left behind enormous deposits of potassium-rich minerals, hidden underground for millions of years.
Developing those deposits presented engineering challenges. Water-bearing rock made sinking mine shafts difficult, requiring new techniques and persistence.
But Canadian miners and engineers found a way.
Communities such as Esterhazy, Rocanville and Lanigan grew alongside the industry as exploration pushed west on the old yellow-head trail, while Saskatchewan became a global potash powerhouse, today accounting for roughly one-third of the world’s supply.
A mineral buried beneath the Canadian Prairies helps grow food on farms from Brazil to India and China.
That’s Canadian mining making a difference on a truly global scale.
And now there’s another kind of buried treasure in Saskatchewan: six ounces of gold waiting for someone who can solve the mystery.
Could Saskatchewan’s potash history lead you to six ounces of gold? Read the original story and watch the embedded video to begin solving the clues.
Read the Saskatchewan treasure story: The Buried Treasure That Fed the World
Manitoba’s fictional hero
Few countries have as many unusual place names as Canada. Indeed, none have a story quite like Flin Flon, a mining community named after a character in an adventure novel.
Roaming a remote northern Manitoba lake in 1914, prospector Tom Creighton discovered copper-bearing rock along the shore.
Soon it came time to name the claim, and Creighton and his partners drew inspiration from The Sunless City , a 1905 novel featuring a character named Josiah Flintabbatey Flonatin.
Thankfully, someone decided to shorten the name, and Flin Flon was born.
Generations of workers and their families were supported by the discovery, which led to a mining district that produced copper, zinc, gold and silver.
Out near Snow Lake, another important mining centre emerged. Long before that, Manitoba’s gold-mining history stretched back even earlier, including the development of the Star Lake gold mine in 1910.
Driven by early prospectors and today’s advanced mines, Manitoba’s mining history is filled with adventure, perseverance and remarkable characters.
Beyond doubt, it’s a story worthy of a novel.
And with a hidden treasure of six ounces of gold still waiting in Manitoba, the mystery continues. Read between the lines, and perhaps the next chapter will feature you.
Think you can solve Manitoba’s mining mystery? Follow the original story and watch its accompanying video for clues that could lead you to the gold.
Read the Manitoba treasure story: Where a Storybook Hero Led Canada to One of Its Greatest Mining Camps
Sudbury’s cosmic collision
If you think Canada’s mining history is full of extraordinary stories, consider this one.
About 1.85 billion years ago, an enormous object from space slammed into what is now northern Ontario.
The impact helped create the geological conditions responsible for one of the greatest concentrations of nickel, copper and platinum-group metals on Earth.
Fast-forward to the 1880s, when railway construction helped reveal the region’s extraordinary mineral wealth.
What followed transformed Sudbury into one of the world’s great mining centres.
Companies such as Inco and Falconbridge became internationally recognized names, while generations of miners, engineers and their families built a city whose identity became inseparable from the industry.
Sudbury’s nickel helped make the stainless steel and alloys used around the world, while its copper and other metals contributed to everything from electrical infrastructure to advanced manufacturing.
Today, the region remains central to Canada’s ambitions in critical minerals, clean technology and advanced industrial production.
And Sudbury has another success story: the transformation of a landscape once scarred by industrial activity into a global example of environmental restoration.
Few places better illustrate mining’s past, present and future.
Somewhere in the Sudbury region, six ounces of gold remain hidden.
Could that cosmic collision lead you to gold here on Earth?
Can Sudbury’s extraordinary geological history point you toward hidden gold? Read the original story and watch the embedded video for clues that could lead you to the treasure.
Read the Sudbury treasure story: The Basin That Built a Mining Nation
And then there’s the big one.
Four regional treasures would be exciting enough.
But the greatest prize of all remains out there.
Somewhere in Canada, 217 1-oz. gold coins are waiting to be discovered.
The grand prize is the centrepiece of the Great Canadian Treasure Hunt, an adventure that has already sent tens of thousands of Canadians poring over maps, researching mining history and debating the meaning of cryptic clues.
The prize is extraordinary.
But so is the journey.
Every clue offers another opportunity to discover something fascinating about this country: a forgotten gold rush, a legendary prospector, a community built around a discovery or a mineral that changed Canadian history.
And remember, you don’t need to be a geologist or experienced prospector to participate. You need curiosity, persistence and a willingness to learn.
You might even discover that the greatest adventures begin with a question.
Next chapter begins
As we look ahead to another year of the Great Canadian Treasure Hunt, we’re excited to continue sharing the stories of the people, places and discoveries that made Canada one of the world’s great mining nations. Hunters and observers alike can look forward to the extension of the hunt into 2027 as so many incredible stories still wait to be told.
There are more communities to celebrate, more characters to meet and more opportunities to inspire the next generation of Canadians.
Because mining isn’t simply part of our past.
It’s essential to our future.
The metals and minerals beneath our feet will help power our homes, build our infrastructure, strengthen our economy and create opportunities for generations to come.
And if the first year of the Great Canadian Treasure Hunt has taught us anything, it’s that Canadians love a good adventure — especially when there’s a chance to discover something new along the way.
So gather your family, call a friend, dust off those maps and start exploring.
There are still five treasures out there – and more to come.
The history is real. The gold is real. And the adventure is far from over.
Visit treasure.northernminer.com to join the Hunt, explore the stories and start solving the clues.
Happy hunting, Canada!

The J29 Toyota Supra and G29 BMW Z4 Are Officially Sold Out in the US Market

Photo: BMW
Internally referred to as J29 and G29, the current generations of the Supra and Z4 have finally disappeared from US new car inventories. Magna Steyr, the contract manufacturer that used to make them, wrapped up the program back in March 2026. Dealers nationwide have exhausted remaining stock, marking the end of an era for both Toyota and BMW.
CarsDirect reported on this first, with CarsDirect also highlighting that both companies prepared for the bitter end as early as April 2025. That's when Toyota introduced the Final Edition of the GR Supra, with BMW following suit in December 2025.
Considering that two-door sports cars are hard to sell nowadays, their US-market figures leave much to be desired. Throughout 2025, the rear-drive models racked up a pitiful 5,066 deliveries. To understand how bad that figure is, the aging ND Miata sold 8,727 units.
In the first nine months of 2026, the Supra and Z4 clocked 2,437 and 1,983 deliveries, respectively. Given the aforementioned, the ND-generation Miata will once again outsell them. Per Mazda's September 2026 report, both the canvas-topped model and the RF totaled 7,598 deliveries in the first three quarters.
All in all, it's a disappointing end for two models that would not have been possible had BMW and Toyota not agreed to join forces. The J29-generation Supra gave the Japanese automaker a compact rear-drive coupe with a turbo'd inline-six, while BMW stuck to the Z4's traditional formula.
Photo: Toyota Developing a dedicated sports car platform independently would have been a poor financial decision, as evidenced by the most recent sales volumes in the US market. Sharing the engineering, meanwhile, gave both parties a way to keep these relatively low-volume models commercially viable.
BMW debuted the Z4 first, with the G29 making its first public appearance in August 2018 at the Pebble Beach Concours d'Elegance. 2019 was the first model year in the United States of America. The GR Supra, meanwhile, went live at the 2019 North American International Auto Show in Detroit. As such, the fixed-head J29 went on sale for the 2020 model year.
Both models offered inline-four options, and both also featured manual options. The manual for the inline-six lump had to wait a little, and truth be told, I wouldn't have either model in any other way. Think about it for a minute. Who in the world is okay with ponying up a lot of money for a four-pot manual Z4 when the MX-5 offers a more organic experience at a lower price?
Toyota was the first to join the BMW-sourced I6 engine with a manual, with BMW following suit. The German partner called the Z4 M40i with said tranny Handschalter, which is German for hand shifter.
The Z4 and Supra are both gone from their respective online configurators, and the Z4 won't return anytime soon. Over at 'Yota, the sixth-generation Supra is moving away from BMW to become an in-house Gazoo Racing project. To be revealed by the end of the decade, the newcomer should feature a new 2.0-liter turbo inline-four capable of more than 400 ponies.

In all seriousness though, the C8 Corvette is a great-looking car. Basically anything higher than a Z06 will offer you this ultra-aggressive widebody aesthetic that you don't necessarily get with the regular Stingray. And when the spec is black-over-black, well, I don't think it gets much better than that to be honest, especially with those $16,000 carbon fiber wheels.
Altogether, this car here retailed for a whopping $261,104 and until yesterday, it had been up for grabs at auction where it failed to sell. The reason why this car doesn't belong to someone else is because the seller, a dealer out of Chicago, refused to let it go for "just" $305,000. I can understand their reasoning. Stock Chevy Corvette E-Ray Walks Into a Speed Shop, Drives Away With 850 HP, and a Supercharger
26 photos
Photo: YouTube/Late Model Racecraft
The Corvette E-Ray was Chevrolet’s first attempt at making America’s Sportscar accustomed to the dawning era of electrical upgrades. As a result, the fabled mid-engined C8 received an e-motor for the front axle, adding 160 extra hp to the V8’s output. One thing led to another, and now the ZR1X is killing hypercars like there’s a bounty of their heads. In the meantime, one E-Ray owner has decided natural aspirations are not high enough for his expectations, and put a blower on his car.
When automotive engineers first pitched hybrid powertrains to the public, the concept was romanticized as the ultimate mechanical lovechild of the internal-combustion and electric worlds, destined to inherit the finest genes from both parents.
As it turned out, the frugal Toyota Prius was never going to be every enthusiast's cup of tea, so the technology soon adopted a fiercely aggressive persona that prioritized blistering velocity over miserly fuel economy calculations.
That philosophical transformation ignited in 2013 through three European hypercars that reshaped performance engineering forever. Ferrari built 499 Coupes of the LaFerrari, pairing a 6.3-liter V12 with electric assist for 950 horsepower (963 PS).
Simultaneously, McLaren assembled 375 examples of its 3.8-liter V8 twin-turbocharged P1 delivering 903 horsepower (916 PS), including 177 from an e-motor, while Porsche crafted 918 all-wheel-drive units of the 887-horsepower (899-PS) 918 Spyder (4.6-liter aspirated V8 plus 179 electric hp).
Photo: YouTube/Late Model Racecraft Those pioneers spawned an entire dynasty of electrified exotics across the decade. Ferrari unleashed the 986-horsepower (1,000-PS) 4.0-liter SF90 Stradale, the 819-horsepower (830-PS) 3.0-liter 296 GTB, and the 1,184-horsepower (1,200-PS) F80, while McLaren introduced the 690-horsepower (700-PS) 3.0-liter Artura and 1,258-horsepower (1,275-PS) W1.
Lamborghini answered with the 808-horsepower (819-PS) Sián, the 1,001-horsepower (1,015-PS) 6.5-liter V12 Revuelto, and the 907-horsepower (920-PS) Temerario, whereas Porsche launched its 532-horsepower (541-PS) 3.6-liter 911 GTS.
Naturally, America refused to watch this high-voltage revolution from the sidelines, and the eighth-generation Chevrolet Corvette E-Ray was born as the first electrified, all-wheel-drive model in Corvette history. Behind the cabin sits GM's naturally aspirated 6.2-liter LT2 pushrod V8, which independently generates 495 horsepower (502 PS) at 6,450 rpm and 470 lb-ft (637 Nm) of torque at 5,150 rpm while driving the rear axle via an 8-speed dual-clutch gearbox.
Photo: YouTube/Late Model Racecraft Up front, a permanent-magnet electric motor draws energy from a self-charging 1.9-kWh lithium-ion battery pack in the center tunnel for 160 horsepower (162 PS) and 125 lb-ft (169 Nm) of torque. Combined, the factory E-Ray produces 655 horsepower (664 PS) and 595 lb-ft (807 Nm) of torque, sprinting from 0 to 60 mph (97 kph) in 2.5 seconds and covering the quarter-mile in 10.5 seconds at 130 mph (209 kph).
Even with those blistering showroom credentials, a dedicated segment of the gearhead population firmly believes that factory output figures are merely a conservative baseline and that there is always room for improvement. Enter Steven Fereday and his crew at Texas tuning powerhouse Late Model Racecraft, where turning stock Corvettes into supercar-slaying monsters is a daily craft demonstrated at their proving grounds.
The subject of their latest showcase is a pristine 2025 Corvette E-Ray Coupe owned by a returning Texas customer, Greg Manning. A while back, the shop built his seventh-generation Corvette Z06 with an 800-horsepower (811-PS) package before upgrading it with a Magnuson supercharger that pulled relentlessly across the tachometer. Hooked on forced induction, Mr. Manning purchased this low-mileage 2025 E-Ray and stored it until the speed shop could work its magic.
Photo: YouTube/Late Model Racecraft Once completed with Late Model Racecraft's signature supercharger package, Mr. Manning's hybrid coupe delivers a combined 850 horsepower (862 PS) at the flywheel and around 583 rear-wheel horsepower (608 PS). That represents a reliable 150-rear-wheel-horsepower (152-PS) gain on 91-octane or 93-octane pump fuel. Anchoring the build is a Magnuson 2650 supercharger featuring a taller lid that flows enough air for 10 to 15 extra horsepower.
Fitting a roots-style blower into a tight mid-engine bay requires intricate engineering: watch Zach, the shop technician, demonstrate this before installation. The Magnuson 2650 system relies on an auxiliary jackshaft assembly that bolts onto the cylinder head over alignment pins, linking the factory serpentine belt system on one side to a dedicated blower drive pulley and idlers. Two internal intercooler bricks, an expansion tank, and an upgraded heat exchanger prevent heat soak.
Before reaching the Texas facility, Mr. Manning's coupe had already received a bespoke rear fascia conversion that reshaped the lower valance to accommodate a center-exit stainless-steel cat-back exhaust system modeled after the eighth-generation Corvette Z06. This setup allows the 6.2-liter pushrod V8 roar to harmonize with the supercharger whine. Aftermarket lowering springs drop the metallic maroon body and tan cabin over custom wheels.
Photo: YouTube/Late Model Racecraft Mechanical hardware only tells half the story, as Late Model Racecraft's proprietary calibration of the Engine Control Module and Transmission Control Module unlocks the platform's true capability. According to Steven Fereday, cracking the 8-speed dual-clutch transmission software eliminated the clutch slip that previously limited modified mid-engine Corvettes.
Furthermore, their calibration enables automatic upshifts at peak engine speed even in Manual Mode, freeing drivers from watching the tachometer during full-throttle sprints.
Out on the pavement, Track Mode on, and disabled traction control, the force-fed electro-ICE ‘Vette executes violent second-gear roll pulls from 30 mph (48 kph) at 4,000 rpm. With the front electric motor pulling alongside 600 rear-wheel horsepower (608 PS), the all-wheel-drive chassis hooks immediately in a perfect blend of electric motor hum, blower whine, and exhaust thunder.
Photo: YouTube/Late Model Racecraft Should Mr. Manning crave more within the next 12 months, further upgrades await. Thailand’s Ministry of Defence began fielding a new computerized rifle trigger designed to help soldiers shoot down small drones, according to last month’s announcement by the device’s manufacturer, Israel Weapon Industries , or IWI. Company officials consider the deployment a real-world endorsement of the Arbel Anti-Drone System as a potential solution for countering drones on the battlefield.
In an interview with Defense News, Semion Dukhan, IWI’s marketing director, described common counter-drone options such as lasers , high-powered electronics , interceptors and specialized ammunition as “not viable in the long run.” He argued that while these technologies can be effective, they often have limitations involving cost, mobility or ease of use. Arbel’s advantage, he said, is its practicality.
“The Arbel is putting a computer to the trigger mechanism of the weapon, so in the context of an anti-drone rifle, what we do is we put the computer in the lower receiver of a standard AR-15 rifle … and with this computer, we control the trigger mechanism of the weapon,” Dukhan said.
He explained that Arbel functions somewhat like a fully automatic weapon in that depressing and holding the trigger engages the system. “So you as an operator, the first bullet that you will shoot, will be purely mechanical … and from the second bullet onward, the system controls the rate of fire to a specific rate of fire that we analyzed as optimal,” he said.
An IWI spokesman says the Arbel trigger device will fit with any standard AR-15 lower receiver. (IWI)
Dukhan said IWI determined the “optimal” rate by analyzing thousands of test shots. “We came down to the specific figure … to get the most chances to hit this kind of target,” he said, describing a target measuring 10 to 15 inches in diameter and flying at roughly 60 kilometers per hour at ranges of 150 to 200 meters.
When IWI unveiled Arbel in 2024, the company said it was intended to improve marksmanship under stressful conditions. Early promotional videos show an operator depressing and holding the trigger before Arbel releases rounds once the system determines the conditions are right.
Dukhan explained that the original version calculates stability and range before discharging a round, whereas the anti-drone version uses an algorithmically calculated rate of fire. “For the anti-drone, it’s only timing. When you, as a user, use the anti-drone algorithm and put it on the Arbel anti-drone safety position, then it only works on timing,” he said.
He added that the option is more “predictable” than the stability-based version, leaving the operator to focus on aiming and following the target. He argued that Arbel can turn anyone with a rifle into a counter-drone operator.
Before Thailand, approximately 25 other countries had already adopted the Arbel system for improving marksmanship or countering drones, according to IWI.

(Saildrone)
PARIS — Saildrone and Norwegian shipbuilding company Umoe Mandal have signed an agreement to produce unmanned surface vessels , with some parts being built in Norway, company executives said.
Under the agreement, signed Wednesday at the Euronaval defense show here, the Norwegian company will build the vessel for Saildrone’s 20-meter-long Surveyor USV, and the US-based manufacturer will provide the autonomy suite as well as electronics and navigation systems.
“The Saildrone Surveyor will provide persistent maritime domain awareness in strategically important waters, including the Baltic and North Seas, as well as Arctic waters, while giving customers sovereign control over their operations and data,” Robert Kleist, Saildrone’s European managing director, told reporters here.
The representative added that Umoe Mandal was selected for its expertise in composite structures, such as glass or carbon fiber. Among other things, the Norwegian company supplies the mast for the British Type-26 frigates.
The agreement is the latest in a series of moves by Saildrone to expand into Europe. Over the summer, the company opened a new headquarters in Copenhagen and, in August, signed an agreement with Polish company Southern Spars to produce Surveyor’s wings in Poland.
Umoe Mandall CEO Tom Fidgeland told reporters that his company has already begun building a new manufacturing site near its main plant, dedicated to producing the USVs.
“This is to answer the demand we know will come in the future. We are doing this without having concrete orders [yet] in place, but we are confident this will be the case based on future work. … We can easily reach two vessels a month, but that can be expanded more than that for sure,” Fidgeland said.
Kleist cited Northern European countries, including Denmark, Finland, Sweden, and Norway, as anticipated interested parties for Saildrone USVs, which could be facilitated through the Nordic Defence Cooperation (NORDEFCO) framework agreement.
The NORDEFCO agreement allows Nordic nations — Norway, Denmark, Finland and Iceland — to rapidly procure different types of systems, including USVs. It follows a sort of surveillance-as-a-service model: instead of buying physical USVs, member countries can contract Saildrone to deliver maritime intelligence.
In October, the Swedish Armed Forces became the first country to execute a national deployment under the NORDEFCO framework , launching a year-long maritime surveillance mission in the Baltic Sea using 4 four Saildrone-made Voyager USVs. In this context, Saildrone operates the vessels, which sail under the Swedish flag, and the Swedish Navy chooses the mission parameters and receives a continuous stream of data.
Kleist said that if other countries opted to adopt this model, it could benefit the regional allies, as they would essentially be looking at the same information, for instance, surveillance of Baltic Sea activities, and could potentially share intelligence among nations as well.
The Baltic Sea is a key maritime area for Europe, as it connects many shipping routes and critical underwater infrastructure. Some countries have vocalized increased concerns over the protection of such infrastructure, with the rise of hybrid warfare and sabotage incidents seen in Europe in recent months. In addition, Russia has direct access to the Baltic Sea through several entry points: Saint Petersburg and the Leningrad Oblast in the east, as well as through the Kaliningrad exclave — situated between Poland and Lithuania.
When asked whether the companies were worried about Russian forces seizing one of the USVs, Fidgeland said they must consider it, but are not concerned it would happen.
“We have radars, we have cameras… We can see them [Russians] miles away. If they have bad intentions, we can take nice photographs of them,” Fidgeland told Breaking Defense.

This Fiat Ducato Camper Van Shows How You Can Maximize Comfort and Style in a Compact Footprint
17 photos
Photo: SüdBadenVan/miniCampers
Much like the Mercedes-Benz Sprinter dominates the campervan landscape in the United States, the Fiat Ducato serves as the primary backbone of the European campervan market. With its robust build, car-like driveability, boxy, conversion-friendly shape, and generous interior headroom, it stands as the most popular choice when it comes to conversion base vehicles.
The light commercial vehicle is highly prominent across SüdBadenVan’s lineup, and the 2027 Schauinsland 540 camper van shows that even the shortest variant of the Fiat Ducato can be turned into a comfortable living space.
Built for travelers who want their camper van to feel more like a small home than a conventional RV, the Schauinsland 540 preserves an open floor plan and combines it with modern amenities and a cozy country-house-inspired aesthetic that creates a warm, inviting atmosphere, setting it apart from standard, sterile conversions.
SüdBadenVan is a boutique German campervan manufacturer based in Umkirch, near Freiburg. It was founded in 2021 and specializes in transforming standard panel vans into functional, premium mobile homes, with an emphasis on sustainability, minimalism, and practical design. The company’s Schauinsland lineup shows how these principles translate into practice, offering a practical mobile habitat for two people.
Photo: SüdBadenVan/miniCampers The Schauinsland 540 is one of the first floorplans introduced by the German company and is built on the shortest length variant of the Fiat Ducato. It measures just 541 cm (17.7 feet) in length, but the interior layout efficiently utilizes the available space to provide comfort, utility, and flexibility for life on the road.
One of the defining traits of the Schauinsland 540 is its open interior layout. There is no solid divider wall behind the driver’s cab, which is always a good choice for compact interiors, as it not only allows easy access from front to back and vice versa, but it also makes the interior feel more spacious and airier.
Instead of dedicating a large portion of the available floor space to a permanent internal bathroom, SüdBadenVan has chosen a more minimalist yet practical approach, with a functional kitchen, a generous seating and dining setup that transforms into a comfortable bed, and ample storage integrated throughout.
This configuration might seem incomplete for some, especially if they plan to adopt a nomad lifestyle full-time, but it frees up precious square footage for a larger kitchen, extra seating, and a bigger bed. However, the Schauinsland 540 doesn’t lack sanitary conveniences altogether. A Trelino composting toilet is still included in a dedicated compartment and slides out only when needed. Optional dry or sealing toilets are also available, and travelers who prefer a more conventional setup can opt for the Schauinsland 540 D , which integrates a wet bathroom.
Photo: SüdBadenVan/miniCampers The open layout allows for seamless transitions between the living, kitchen, and sleeping areas. At the front, the cab seats swivel all the way around to add extra seating space, and the nearby kitchen is well-equipped for fresh home-cooked meals.
It features a 1,800-watt induction cooktop, a stainless steel sink with a folding faucet, and a 70-liter compressor refrigerator, neatly integrated into a suspended cabinet. The water storage is deliberately kept compact and flexible. Instead of permanent tanks, the company equipped the van with a 20-liter fresh water tank and a 20-liter waste water tank, positioned directly under the sink. Both are removable, making them easier to handle when filling or emptying.
Photo: SüdBadenVan/miniCampers At the rear, the Schauinsland 540 camper van features a versatile seating and sleeping area. During the day, you get a U-shaped sofa with a round, height-adjustable table in the middle, creating a nice setup for dining, lounging, and spending time indoors.
At night, the opposing sofas can be used as two longitudinal beds measuring approximately 180 x 70 cm (70 x 27.5 inches) and 200 x 70 cm (79 x 27.5 inches), respectively, or can be combined to form a much larger sleeping surface of around 200 by 180 cm (79 by 70 inches). If more sleeping capacity is needed, an optional pop-up roof transforms the Schauinsland 540 into a four-berth camper.
Because many travelers view their vehicles not just as a means of travel , but as genuine living spaces, the aesthetics aspect is really important. The team at SüdBadenVan seems to understand its clients’ need for a homey vibe, and for this camper van, they used a combination of wooden surfaces, light finishes, and soft upholstery to create a country-house ambiance reminiscent of a small chalet on wheels.
Photo: SüdBadenVan/miniCampers The kitchen counters, cabinet fronts, and rear tabletop, for instance, are finished in Swiss stone pine, which, with its fine grain and dark knots, brings warmth to the living space. The plank-style ceiling paneling and grey felt material on the side walls further enhance the cozy, warm ambiance, while the high-quality mattresses, available with fabric or corduroy covers, add another residential touch.
The built-in cabinetry inside this van is made from waterproof bonded lightweight plywood, while the cabinet fronts and window frames feature multiplex construction with genuine Swiss stone pine veneer. The rig is designed for all-season use with 19mm Vanue insulation, vinyl flooring with impact-sound insulation, and a 2-kW Autoterm diesel parking heater with ComfortControl functionality.
For electrical independence, the camper van is equipped with an EcoFlow PowerHub, which delivers 3,600 watts of AC output (or up to 5,200 watts with X-Boost). The system incorporates an integrated charging booster and shore power charger, along with two solar charge controllers for fixed and mobile solar installations.
Photo: SüdBadenVan/miniCampers A selection of optional features is also available and includes a pop-top roof with integrated lighting and a mattress, a larger EcoFlow battery, a 5G WLAN router for internet connectivity, a Dometic FlyTec insect screen door, extra roof hatches, and more.
It’s also worth mentioning that the base vehicle comes standard with a 140-hp engine paired with a manual transmission, but buyers can upgrade to a 180-hp engine with an automatic gearbox as well. And for those who want to venture into the wilderness, an off-road package is also available, featuring all-season tires and Fiat's Traction+ system.
As for pricing, the 2027 SüdBadenVan Schauinsland 540 camper van starts at €89,000 ($99.880), but the custom options and upgrades will push the total higher.

Photo: Mercedes-Benz
When you're driving a German luxobarge that weighs more than two metric tons, you expect the brakes to work perfectly so, every time, regardless of conditions. Over at Mercedes, the front brake hoses of an estimated 215,231 vehicles may leak brake fluid without any warning.
Per the Federal Motor Transport Authority of Germany, the S-Class recall is referred to as 17121R as opposed to 4391103 in Mercedes lingo. Affected models were produced over five years, from June 2019 all the way to November 2024. The KBA says that 11,828 suspect vehicles were registered in the automaker's home market.
Recall documentation reveals that 223-series luxury sedans equipped with air suspension are being recalled, including Maybach and AMG versions of the Sonderklasse. It should be mentioned that AIRMATIC is completely standard, replacing conventional metal coil springs with compressed air-filled rubber struts.
For model year 2027, suspension options include the cloud-connected Intelligent AIRMATIC setup and the optional E-ACTIVE BODY CONTROL. The former can pre-adjust its damping electronically before reaching any road imperfection due to V2X tech.
Available on higher configurations, E-ACTIVE BODY CONTROL builds on the Intelligent AIRMATIC suspension with 48-volt hydraulic actuators located above the air springs, front stereo cameras that actively read the road, and CURVE mode.
Regarding the latter, CURVE means the massive Sonderklasse can bank into turns like a motorcycle to neutralize lateral forces. CURVE also keeps the body flat under acceleration and braking.
Photo: Mercedes-Benz Given that air suspension covers all versions of the 223 series, that means the Maybach S 680 and the AMG S 63 E PERFORMANCE feature potentially suspect brake hoses. Those hoses carry brake fluid while accommodating wheel movement. Using rubber hoses is a must due to the movement of the wheels, suspension, and steering system.
Leaking hydraulic fluid understandably compromises braking performance, increasing the braking distance. When you're going crazy fast on unrestricted sections of the Autobahn, this kind of leak can end in a big crash because the driver is not accustomed to the reduced braking performance caused by a potential hydraulic fluid leak from said hoses.
Worse still, escaping brake fluid reaches the surface of the road, creating a hazard for vehicles following behind. Transport Canada published a localized safety recall in October 2026, and its guidance warns that brake pedal travel and feel can change dramatically when a leak occurs.
For affected owners, regardless of their country of residence, contacting Mercedes customer service or the nearest dealer is the best course of action. Customers should not interpret the absence of brake fluid on the front hoses and adjacent parts as proof that their vehicles do not fall within this campaign.
Germany's Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt and the US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration both identify Continental as the supplier of the suspect hoses. The subject components fail to meet durability specifications when subjected to mechanical and thermal stress, causing the hoses to develop leaks over time.

Packsize and Swisslog are partnering to build on-demand box making into automated warehouse systems. The companies will help customers design how goods move from storage and picking through packing and shipping , with Swisslog overseeing the integration.
What’s Related
Packsize supplies equipment that makes shipping boxes sized to each order. Swisslog designs the systems that store goods, retrieve them, and bring them to picking stations. Under the agreement, the companies will plan those steps together so customers can decide where boxes should be made and when they need to reach workers as orders move through the warehouse.
“As fulfillment operations become increasingly automated, the inclusion of packaging automation in a holistic warehouse automation design has never been more important,” said Bill Stenger, senior vice president of sales at Swisslog. Packsize said the goal is to reduce how often workers handle orders, cut packaging waste, and help warehouses ship more orders.
RELATED STORIES: The Power of the Perfect Box Design | Swisslog Launches FastMove Monorail System for Pallet Transport
How Picking and Packing Work Together
At a warehouse that makes boxes to order, the box can be ready by the time the items reach a picking station. Workers can then put the items straight into the box that will ship to a customer or store. That can save a transfer at the packing station, and a closer-fitting box can reduce the filler needed to keep items from shifting.
Packsize said the companies have already worked together on multiple projects. The announcement did not name any new customers or provide pricing or a rollout schedule.
How Northern Tool Uses the Setup
At Northern Tool + Equipment’s South Carolina distribution center , Swisslog connected the retailer ’s existing Packsize equipment to an AutoStore system. Swisslog’s SynQ software coordinates the two so a custom box reaches the right workstation when the items for that order are ready to pick. The same stations handle orders headed to customers and to stores.
After picking, workers seal, label, and weigh the boxes to check for errors before shipping. According to a Swisslog case study, Northern Tool previously checked each order against its invoice by hand before sealing the box.
Swisslog said the wider automation project freed up nearly 50,000 square feet by replacing a three-level picking area. The company also reported lower freight and packing costs from making boxes to fit each order. At Northern Tool, the retailer already had the box-making equipment. The change was connecting it to picking so workers had the right carton when they needed it.

MUNICH — The Eurofighter consortium is eyeing global market “opportunities” to sell more than 200 of the multirole fighter jets , an infographic shared by the consortium during the International Fighter Conference showed.
Potential new deals of the combat aircraft include second batch orders for Turkey and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, jointly amounting to 78 units, while closing an order from Austria would add a further 36 aircraft.
A breakdown of customers and associated aircraft quantities representing 86 or more aircraft from the 200-plus projection was not shared, but the consortium has long expressed interest in exporting to countries like Portugal, Poland and Bangladesh.
Portugal is in need of replacing a fleet of aging F-16 fighter jets, with a successor solution pitting Eurofighter, Lockheed Martin’s F-35, Sweden’s Gripen and France’s Rafale against one another . Airbus is leading the Eurofighter consortium’s sales campaign with Lisbon.
“Our proposal offering the Eurofighter Typhoon to replace Portugal’s F-16 fleet is currently in its final stages of preparation,” an Airbus spokesperson told Breaking Defense in a statement today. “To capture the full spectrum of operational sovereignty, life-cycle value, and industrial collaboration opportunities for the Portuguese Government and national industry, the comprehensive proposal will be formally submitted by the end of this year.”
Similarly, Warsaw is eyeing a contract to acquire 32 additional fighter jets in support of an air superiority program requirement. However, it could decide to procure more US F-35 fighter jets after securing a $4 billion Foreign Military Financing (FMF) loan from Washington in September.
Last year, Italy’s Leonardo and the Bangladesh air force signed a letter of intent aimed at opening talks on a Eurofighter deal with Bangladesh, but Dhaka has also moved toward negotiating with China over an acquisition of rival J-10CE fighter jets, according Reuters report .
The number of potential exports for Eurofighter has increased from last year’s figure of 134 units, shared at the 2025 edition of the International Fighter Conference. At the time, Eurofighter CEO Tamarit Degenhardt told Breaking Defense that Turkey’s initial order for the multirole combat jet could serve as a “ wake-up call ” for other nations to ink new deals.
In 2025, Turkey signed a $10.7 billion deal with the UK for the acquisition of 20 Typhoons, solidifying a prior MoU between the two nations for a total of 40 aircraft.
As for current manufacturing developments, additional figures shared this week at the conference indicate that 60 aircraft are currently in production as the consortium executes contracts with Spain, Germany and Kuwait.
Recent orders including the Turkish deal, amount to 89 aircraft set for future production and in line with acquisitions from Spain (Halcon 2), Germany (Tranche 5) and Italy.
No update was provided relating to plans for a production ramp up, but Degenhardt noted last year that he is targeting a rate of 30 aircraft a year beginning in 2028 — based on securing new export business.

Evommune is commiting $30 million upfront for Hinova Pharmaceuticals’ oral molecular glue degrader—a low-cost bet with a high probability of success, according to analysts, after clinical failures roiled the biotech’s internal pipeline earlier this year.
Evommune is paying Hinova Pharmaceuticals $30 million to license the China biopharma’s oral molecular glue degrader for autoimmune diseases.
The pact gives Evommune worldwide rights—excluding in the Greater China area—to a VAV1-directed candidate, with a mid-stage trial in rheumatoid arthritis slated to launch in 2027.
Evommune’s upfront payment consists of $20 million cash and $10 million in pre-funded warrants to purchase Evommune stock, according to a Thursday release . Hinova could also garner up to $1.1 billion in milestone payments, plus royalties on net sales outside of China.
The molecular glue degrader, formerly called HC118 and known as HP570 in China, will now be called EVO570. Requests to begin clinical trials for the drug have been accepted in the U.S. and submitted in China, with a Phase 1 study expected to launch imminently.
EVO570 targets VAV1, a signaling protein mainly located in immune cells that drives T and B cell activation across several chronic inflammatory diseases, according to the companies. The molecular glue degrader is designed to eliminate VAV1, thereby improving safety and tolerability compared to JAK inhibitor treatments.
Oppenheimer analysts view the “low-cost/high-PoS [probability of success] deal as a major positive advancement” for Evommune, according to a Thursday investor note. As rationale, the analysts cited the creation of a near-term clinical catalyst and the potential for a first-in-class rheumatoid arthritis program, plus the possibility of expansion into neurological indications.
There are over 1.2 million U.S. patients with rheumatoid arthritis, a chronic condition that causes inflammation of the joints. The space carries “significant commercial opportunity that can accommodate multiple players,” according to Oppenheimer. Currently, the only approved oral therapies for the condition are JAK inhibitors, which carry boxed warnings for serious safety risks, such as mortality and thrombosis.
In preclinical studies, EVO570 demonstrated 20 times more potency than Novartis’ oral molecular glue degrader MRT-6160, according to Oppenheimer. Novartis picked up MRT-6160 from Monte Rosa Therapeutics in 2024 for $150 million upfront and up to $2.1 billion biobucks. The asset is currently in mid-stage development for psoriatic arthritis and Sjögren’s disease.
Importantly, the freshly penned deal addresses Evommune’s “catalyst vacuum” after its oral asset EVO756 missed in mid-stage studies for both chronic spontaneous urticaria and atopic dermatitis. Development of the candidate in both indications has been discontinued, though the biotech continues to study the asset in a mid-phase migraine trial.

Evommune ends development of lead asset in chronic hives after mid-stage efficacy woes
With the failure in chronic spontaneous urticaria, Evommune’s story is now centered on its anti-IL-18 therapy EVO301, Oppenheimer said, which in February elicited a 33% placebo-adjusted improvement in eczema severity.

Humble Robotics raised a $51 million Series A on Thursday to move its cabless, electric Humble Hauler into customer pilots on port drayage and warehouse runs. Obvious Ventures led the round, with participation from existing investors Eclipse and Energy Impact Partners.
The raise brings the San Francisco startup’s total funding to $75 million, about six months after it emerged from stealth with a $24 million seed round and a driverless truck built with no cab . It also funds a bet founder and CEO Eyal Cohen made after a decade on long-haul autonomy: that short, repeatable freight moves, such as port drayage and plant-to-warehouse shuttles, are a more controlled place to put driverless, electric trucks to work than the open highway.
The new money will pay for customer pilots, testing and validation, early manufacturing, and a broader family of vehicles built on Humble’s modular platform, the company said in its release. Humble told FreightWaves Today in September it plans to sell the haulers to third-party operators.
Humble is targeting regional routes under 250 miles, which it says make up 87% of U.S. truck tonnage. That figure comes from 2021 federal data: trucks moved nearly 12 billion tons of domestic freight that year, and 87% of it traveled less than 250 miles, according to a Department of Energy analysis . Shipments under 100 miles accounted for 44% on their own.
Humble says it is working with customers, partners, and regulators to prepare for commercial deployment.
“We’ve spent years proving that a truck can drive itself. The harder question is how to make autonomy something a freight operator can depend on every day,” Cohen said in the release.
Why Humble picked short runs
Cohen’s long-haul work focused on lanes such as Dallas to Houston and Dallas to El Paso, Texas, he said in an August interview with FreightWaves. Then he looked at short-haul freight, a large market that almost no one was trying to automate.
“Short moves are served very well by electrification. Long haul is tougher in electrification, right? You are trying to figure out a massive battery and a massive charging system,” Cohen said.
The company’s website lists four use cases for the Hauler: port drayage, plant-to-warehouse shuttles, rail yard moves, and short legs between a carrier’s own terminals. It lists a 200-mile maximum range and a 55 mph top speed.
The shorter distance also changes what happens when something goes wrong.
“There are challenges even with the technology working perfectly with sending a large robot a thousand miles away, right? With no margin for error. I mean it has to be very safe,” Cohen said. “And in shorter distances that’s just a more controlled situation. You could have a depot nearby. You can have engineers nearby.”
A hauler with no cab or hitch
A conventional drayage move uses a day cab tractor pulling a container on a chassis. A lot of autonomous trucking automates only the tractor, Cohen said. That leaves two problems: something has to make the connection, and the tractor’s sensors can’t see behind the trailer.
“Today, if you have a tractor and you want to hook a trailer to it, you have to somehow automate that connection, right? That is non-trivial and I think people have been working on that for a while,” Cohen said. “People are using robotic arms and other mechanisms to try to connect a trailer to a tractor. Very challenging, right?”
Cohen’s answer was to combine the two into one flat, skateboard-style platform. Its standard configuration carries 40-foot international and 53-foot domestic containers, and sensor pods with cameras, lidar, and radar give it a 360-degree view, according to the company’s site.
The design started from a question Cohen asked himself: what would a freight vehicle look like if the autonomy were perfect?
“If you had a quantum computer and this AGI brain, how would you think about moving freight? It would be just a platform, right, that you can land a container on,” he said.
Dropping the cab also drops weight. The website bills the Hauler as 20% lighter than a traditional tractor and trailer, and that freed-up weight is the economic pitch.
“The goal is to take more weight per move if we can to reduce the cost per mile as well,” Cohen said.
Investors return before customer pilots
Eclipse, which led Humble’s seed round, returned for the Series A.
“Modernizing freight requires rethinking the entire system, from the vehicle itself to the intelligence that powers it,” said Jiten Behl, partner at Eclipse.
For scale, Gatik, which already runs autonomous routes of up to 400 miles between distribution centers and stores, raised $200 million in a Series D in August after completing 85,000 fully driverless orders .
But challenges remain. The release names no customers. In August, Cohen said the company was “aiming for customer pilots over the next 12 months.” He also acknowledged that Humble is building electric trucks for a market that has been slow to buy them.
“The electric trucks famously have not really taken off in the United States, but they’re taking off elsewhere internationally,” Cohen said.
Cohen’s path from Otto to Humble
Cohen spent his first decade as an engineer electrifying “buses, tanks, cars, excavators,” then moved to Apple before joining Otto as one of its first engineers. He stayed through Otto’s acquisition by Uber, then worked at Pronto and spent three years at Waabi.
At Otto, he worked on the October 2016 run in which a self-driving truck hauled a load of Budweiser 120 miles down Interstate 25 in Colorado with no one in the driver’s seat, Overdrive noted.
“You could see how amazing the technology could be and you could also see how far away the technology was.” Cohen said.
Handling every case on unpredictable U.S. roads, from a flat tire to a pedestrian on the highway, meant engineers had to hand-code each scenario into the truck, he said. He called 2016 his “reverse aha moment.”
The large language models behind tools like ChatGPT gave him a second aha moment, this one about what the truck’s software could understand. “There is now technology that allows us to reason about the world without having to individually list every single use case out there and try to solve it,” Cohen said. “And that’s been a real change.”
With the new round, Cohen said in the release, Humble is “taking the next step toward safer, more reliable and less expensive operations at scale.”
Why it matters: Why it matters: Drayage fleets that shuttle containers between ports and nearby warehouses could add a driverless option to their equipment plans if Humble’s pilots show the lighter Hauler carries more weight per move. Cohen’s 12-month target for those pilots runs through August 2027.

Aerial view of the Chibougamau drill site. Credit: Central Asia Metals.
Posted By: FREDERIC TOMESCO November 5, 2026
Central Asia Metals ’ (AIM, TSX: CAML) newly acquired Chibougamau project in Quebec could produce more copper annually than the company’s Kounrad mine, helping offset shrinking output at the Kazakhstan operation in the early 2030s, according to BMO Capital Markets.
Annual steady-state production at Chibougamau could hit about 20,000 tonnes of copper and 32,000 oz. of gold, with first output set for late 2031 or early 2032, BMO Capital Markets mining analyst Alexander Pearce said Wednesday in a note. Pearce resumed coverage at outperform, while cutting his share-price target by 25% to 180 pence (C$3.38) from 240 pence. Chibougamau could more than replace the copper output Central Asia expects to lose as Kounrad declines. But that growth would require substantial investment: BMO assumes $450 million (C$630 million) in pre-production capital, including replacement of the existing mill, with permitting likely to determine when construction can begin.
“While the project is early stage and many unknowns remain, its existing infrastructure and potential resource upside via its hub-and-spoke model are key positives,” Pearce wrote.
Central Asia shares rose 2.1% to C$2.41 Thursday morning in Toronto, valuing the company at about C$618 million ($441 million). They’ve ranged between C$2.26 and C$2.59 since the stock began trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange last week.
Three-year build
BMO is assuming Chibougamau will require three years of construction for annual mill throughput of 900,000 tonnes. An updated preliminary economic assessment is expected in the second half of 2027.
Central Asia inherited Chibougamau when it completed its acquisition of Cygnus Metals Oct. 27. Cygnus shareholders received 0.06 Central Asia shares for each share held.
The Canadian project adds potential replacement production as Kounrad declines. An August reserve update forecast copper output at the mine could drop to 9,000 tonnes in 2031 and 6,000 tonnes in 2032, with production continuing through 2034. Central Asia’s 2026 target remains 12,000–13,000 tonnes.
Kounrad recovers copper from historical waste dumps in Kazakhstan. London-based Central Asia also operates the Sasa zinc-lead mine in North Macedonia.
Five deposits
Located about 480 km north of Montreal, Chibougamau covers more than 282 sq. km. Its Copper Rand processing plant last operated in 2008 and has historical capacity of 900,000 tonnes a year. Central Asia says the plant requires refurbishment, but BMO assumes it will be replaced.
The project also has tailings storage, a hydroelectric power connection and road and rail infrastructure. Five deposits — Corner Bay, Devlin, Cedar Bay, Joe Mann and Golden Eye — lie within about 50 km of the plant and could supply a central mill.
A September 2025 estimate for Chibougamau estimated the property holds measured and indicated resources of 6.4 million tonnes grading 2.3% copper, 0.8 gram gold per tonne and 7.6 grams silver per tonne for contained metal of 149,000 tonnes copper, 167,000 oz. gold and about 1.6 million oz. silver.
Inferred resources total 8.5 million tonnes grading 2.1% copper, 1.7 grams gold per tonne and 7.9 grams silver per tonne, containing 182,000 tonnes copper, 454,000 oz. gold and about 2.2 million oz. silver.
No mineral reserves have been established at Chibougamau. Further studies must determine the mine plan, capital requirements and operating costs before BMO’s conceptual production case can be tested.

Supply chain leaders who take electricity for granted may face an expensive surprise.
What’s Related
Gartner said Thursday that access to energy is becoming a major constraint on supply chain growth, as rising electricity demand runs into aging grid infrastructure and slow connection timelines. The research firm predicts that by 2029, most manufacturers without advanced energy management will see costs 20% to 30% higher because of price and supply volatility, network congestion, and capacity constraints.
“Many supply chains continue to operate under the assumption that energy is an always-available input,” said Marta Muñoz, senior director analyst in Gartner’s Supply Chain practice. “That assumption is becoming increasingly difficult to sustain. Energy availability is emerging as a factor that can influence where organizations operate, how they expand , and whether they can execute automation and electrification strategies as planned.”
New demand from AI data centers and electric fleets is hitting a grid that’s already short on transmission capacity. On top of that, getting a new grid connection can be a long process.
MORE FROM GARTNER: Nearly Half of Supply Chains Cut Staff Because of AI | Few Supply Chains Will Let AI Make Planning Calls by 2030
Dealing with grid limits
Most energy management still relies on procurement contracts and assumes the grid will stay as reliable as it has been. Gartner says those strategies do nothing to address physical limits like grid congestion or local capacity shortages. Those limits are starting to shape where companies build and how fast they can grow.
Where the risk shows up
Gartner points to several ways energy constraints can hit operations:
Grid outages can halt manufacturing and distribution.
Long interconnection timelines can delay facility openings and expansions.
Local congestion can drive up facility-level energy costs and squeeze margins.
Limited grid capacity can slow fleet electrification and automation projects.
Suppliers in energy-strapped regions may face higher costs or lower output, and that ripples down the chain.
What to do now
Gartner advises CSCOs to build energy into network design and resilience planning instead of leaving it to procurement.
“CSCOs should begin treating energy availability as a core consideration in network design and growth planning,” said Muñoz. “This means evaluating energy constraints during site selection, aligning energy strategies with local grid realities and incorporating energy availability into broader supply chain resilience efforts.”
In practice, a good first step is asking the local utility about available capacity and connection timelines before you commit to a site. It’s also worth checking which of your key suppliers work in regions where the grid is already strained.
