The big mil was reached in October 2026, a month in which Geely sold a grand total of 71,337 units. All told, averaging one sale every minute in the past couple of years is truly impressive for a vehicle the US market has not experienced. If you ask me, that's even more outstanding when you remember that Geely is the kind of auto brand most of us continue to dismiss as just another Chinese newcomer.
Geely Automobile Holdings Limited of Hangzhou, Zhejiang, launched the EX2 in October 2024, and customers wasted little time getting their own EX2s. The full-electric hatchback reached 10,000 sales within 16 days, then crossed 200,000 deliveries after little more than 200 days. The 600,000th sale was clocked on its 536th day. Commercially successful, alright!
The 2025 result, namely its first full year on sale, was particularly spectacular. No fewer than 465,775 were moved in total, making it the best-selling passenger car in China across all segments and the world's top seller in both the A and B segments. Based on its footprint, the EX2 is more subcompact than city car.
Photo: Geely By October 2026, its maker had introduced the rear-drive hatchback in more than 30 markets across Europe, Africa, the Middle East, Asia-Pacific region, and Latin America. The question is, what made the EX2 so appealing in so many places that could not be more diverse in terms of customer preferences?
I, for one, like cheap and cheerful vehicles as much as the next person. Honest vehicles are rare nowadays, and I also like its warranties. As far as the battery is concerned, and this is the biggest concern you can have with a fully electric vehicle, Geely provides an eight-year warranty up to 200,000 kilometers (124,274 miles). Said warranty applies to the general vehicle as well.
Over those eight years or 200,000 clicks, the battery warranty guarantees at least 70 percent of the original capacity. Regarding prices, how do you feel about 90 euros per month through financing or 99 euros per month via leasing? Retail prices, meanwhile, kick off at 19,990 euros in Germany. That's the largest new car market in Europe, and two grand over the Dacia Spring for a lot more car and standard equipment sounds like a great deal.
Equipped with a multi-link rear suspension instead of a cheapo torsion-beam setup, the EX2 offers 70 liters (2.5 cubic feet) in the front trunk and very flexible rear cargo space. Its quoted turning radius makes it perfect in the urban jungle, and better still, customers are not forced to compromise where it actually matters.
Those who do little, mostly urban driving are presented with a smaller battery (35.35 kWh) that provides 252 kilometers (157 miles) in the WLTP, while customers who need more driving range in one go can opt for a 47.14-kWh pack that promises up to 345 kilometers (214 miles). In both cases, fast charging from 30 to 80 percent should take 25 minutes.
As it stands, Geely and the EX2 now have to prove that the next million will come just as easily as Chinese rivals bring increasingly competitive small EVs to showrooms worldwide. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Geely Australia | New Energy Vehicles (@geely.auto.australia)

Walmart is adding 300 Zipline drone delivery sites under a new multi-year agreement, expanding a service that brings items to customers’ homes in as little as 30 minutes. The deal leaves room for more sites beyond that commitment.
What’s Related
Zipline also announced $1.5 billion in funding to expand its U.S. manufacturing facilities, hire more staff and build a nationwide drone delivery network. The round values the company at $21.5 billion after the investment.
Walmart has worked with Zipline on drone deliveries since 2021. The retailer said its drone delivery program has completed more than 2 million deliveries, including deliveries from Zipline.
From store to home
The expansion builds on Walmart’s stores as starting points for home deliveries. The retailer said 90% of Americans live within 10 miles of a Walmart.
“We see customers try drone delivery for the novelty and then continue to come back to it for the convenience when they need something in minutes,” said Greg Cathey, Walmart’s senior vice president of eCommerce Fulfillment Transformation. “Walmart’s stores put us close to the communities we serve. With Zipline, we can build on that proximity and bring this fast delivery option to even more customers across the country.”
RELATED STORIES: Walmart Expands Drone Delivery to 150 More U.S. Locations | Massachusetts Wants to Hit Pause on Amazon’s Drone Delivery Plans
Customers with eligible addresses can select drone delivery in the Walmart app or on Walmart.com. Customers with eligible addresses can also order through the Zipline app. Tens of thousands of items are eligible.
Deliveries go to a front yard, backyard, or driveway. The aircraft stays roughly 330 feet above the ground while a tether lowers a pod carrying the order.
Drone delivery sits alongside Walmart’s other options, including one-hour-or-less Express delivery and scheduled delivery.
Betting on Speed
Zipline’s pitch to customers and investors is speed. The company said its median order in October arrived 19 minutes after checkout, compared with 30-plus minutes for traditional delivery. Bakery orders were even faster, arriving in a median of 10 minutes.
Zipline said it has made more than 1 million deliveries in Dallas-Fort Worth alone this year. Uber is aiming even higher, targeting 1 million deliveries a day with Zipline by 2029.
The new funding will help Zipline expand its U.S. manufacturing facilities and hire more people, though the company didn’t say how much will go to each or how many jobs it plans to add. Paradigm, WCM Investment Management, and Layer Global led the round, with Uber, Fidelity, and Salesforce Ventures among the other investors.
“Zipline has already brought the future of delivery to the communities it serves. Now, the opportunity is to reach millions more,” said Anton Levy, founder and managing partner of Layer Global.
Other Walmart News
$6 Billion Symbotic Expansion : Walmart committed approximately $6 billion to expand its Symbotic agreement, including additional automation at 25 U.S. regional distribution centers .
Warehouse Automation Challenges : Walmart plans to replace shipping boxes that do not fit its automated systems as its warehouse upgrades face packaging problems, robot repairs and higher electricity costs, according to The Wall Street Journal.
Stockton, California, Fulfillment Center Opens : Walmart opened an automated fulfillment center spanning more than 900,000 square feet to handle West Coast online orders. The facility is expected to create more than 1,000 jobs .
ShipStation Adds Walmart Shipping Rates : ShipStation launched Ship with Walmart, giving U.S. Marketplace sellers access to Walmart-negotiated shipping rates and up to $100 in protection for eligible lost-item claims.
$1.3 Billion Georgia Fulfillment Center Planned : Walmart plans a 1.5 million-square-foot automated fulfillment center in Carnesville, Georgia, expected to create 1,000 jobs. Construction is scheduled to begin in late 2026.

The 2027 Toyota RAV4 is bringing a few major updates, including an added NACS charge port on all plug-in hybrid (PHEV) models.
2027 Toyota RAV4 prices and updates
The RAV4 was Toyota’s best-selling nameplate in the US last year and consistently ranks among America’s most popular vehicles alongside the Ford F-Series and Chevrolet Silverado.
For the 2027 model year, Toyota added several notable upgrades. The 2027 Toyota RAV4 will be available with hybrid (HEV) and plug-in hybrid (PHEV) powertrains, with available front- or all-wheel drive (AWD).
The biggest change is that all 2027 RAV4 PHEV models now have a built-in NACS charge port with Level 3 DC fast-charging capabilities.

The NACS port is on the driver’s side and lets drivers use Tesla Superchargers without a separate adapter. All PHEV grades also include an 11 kW onboard AC charger.
Powered by Toyota’s sixth-generation PHEV system, the plug-in RAV4 has standard AWD with a combined output of 321 horsepower. The setup includes a 2.5-liter four-cylinder engine, two electric motors, and a high-capacity traction battery.
2027 Toyota RAV4 PHEV Woodland (Source: Toyota)
The 2027 Toyota RAV4 PHEV offers up to 52 miles of pure electric range on the base SE trim. It will be available in four trims: SE, XSE, Woodland, and GR Sport.
Toyota updated the suspension system in the Woodland grade for the 2027 model year with new springs, shocks, and jounce bumpers, giving it 9.1″ of ground clearance.
2027 Toyota RAV4 PHEV GR-Sport (Source: Toyota)
The Woodland trim adds a rugged look with standard All-Terrain tires, Roof Rails with Cross Bars, and a Tow Hitch Receiver. It also features new all-weather floor and cargo mats.
Lastly, the RAV4 GR Sport trim is for those who want a more performance-oriented, sporty style, with GT-tuned suspension and steering, sports seating, and a standard PHEV powertrain with AWD.
2027 Toyota RAV4 PHEV GR-Sport interior (Source: Toyota)
Inside, the 2027 RAV4 includes a standard 12.3″ digital cluster and a 10.5″ touchscreen with the Toyota Audio Multimedia system, plus wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.
A 12.9″ touchscreen with a JBL Premium Audio system with 9 speakers is standard on the Limited trim and available on the XSE grade.

Pent-up demand for the new pancreatic cancer therapy Rasonque helped RevMed soar past analysts’ sales expectations and reach 5,000 patients in the third quarter.
Remarkable, historic, impressive, outstanding, stellar—these are a few of the words analysts used to describe the launch of Revolution Medicines’ pancreatic cancer medicine Rasonque.
RevMed reported $198 million in revenue for the asset on Wednesday, despite only five weeks of sales following its late August approval . The value was 10 times Truist Securities’ $19 million estimate.
“‘Que the duck boats,” Truist Securities quipped on Wednesday evening.
That revenue stems from the more than 5,000 patients Rasonque has so far reached, RevMed’s Chief Global Commercialization Officer Anthony Mancini said on a Wednesday afternoon earnings call. The impressive launch reflects pent-up demand for the RAS inhibitor, analysts said, which arrived on the market to cheers from across the industry and beyond.
Patients with pancreatic cancer had few options prior to Rasonque, with the disease among the deadliest forms of cancer . The drug was cleared in August for treating adults with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma who have received at least one prior systemic therapy or are not candidates for multiagent systemic therapy.
Rasonque arrived to “a sizable bolus of treatment option-exhausted patients,” Leerink Partners wrote on Thursday morning.

Specifically, demand was driven by three channels, Mancini explained. First, RevMed worked to convert participants in the Early Access Program (EAP) into commercial patients, an effort that was completed for U.S. users in the quarter. “We prioritized continuity of care and successfully supported patients in obtaining their medication through the transition,” he said.
Then there were those treatment-exhausted patients, who Mancini said included patients who were later in their treatment journey and had been waiting for a new option.
The third pillar was patients newly diagnosed with second-line disease, where RevMed was particularly impressed with uptake.
“We’re encouraged by the speed with which we were able to begin serving patients following approval, which reflects the significant unmet need in metastatic pancreatic cancer, the strength of Rasonque’s clinical profile and label, the strong launch readiness and initial execution across functions as well as payer engagement and patient support in line with our expectations,” Mancini said.
But the commercial chief also sought to temper expectations about how this launch curve may flatten out. “These early results are highly encouraging. At the same time, with only five weeks of commercialization activity, it’s too early to draw conclusions about the normalized trajectory of the launch,” he said. The EAP patients and those awaiting new options in particular represent a “finite” group of patients.
“As our launch matures, revenue will increasingly reflect ongoing treatment for newly eligible patients and ongoing treatment duration,” Mancini said.

Still, analysts were bullish on Rasonque’s growth potential. For the rest of the year, RevMed will look to bring on new patients as they advance to second line treatment for the disease. Leerink revised sales expectations to $440 million for the fourth quarter, compared to $330 million on the high end of previous estimates.
RevMed is still working on insurance coverage for Rasonque as well, Mancini noted.
Meanwhile, RevMed CEO Mark Goldsmith wants to make the drug available all over the world so that all patients with the difficult cancer may benefit. Europe’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP) has issued a positive opinion of the drug, with a formal approval decision pending with the European Medicines Agency.
Digging in
RevMed reported a net loss of $407.5 million for the third quarter, compared to $305.2 million for the same period a year earlier. The company had $3.7 billion in cash on hand as of September 30, not including royalty payments that began flowing from Royalty Pharma in line with Rasonque sales. The company expects to invest deeper into its RAS(ON) inhibitor portfolio while supporting launch efforts for Rasonque into 2027, according to CFO Jack Anders.
Meanwhile, the biotech will also move toward adding additional lines of treatment for Rasonque, including first-line metastatic and resectable disease. Enrollment for the Phase 3 RASolute 303 trial studying the drug alone and with chemotherapy in patients with first-line metastatic pancreatic cancer recently wrapped in the U.S., Chief Development Officer Alan Sadler said on the call. And dosing has begun in another first-line Phase 3 test called RASolute 309, which features patients with RAS G12D pancreatic cancer. This study pairs Rasonque with RevMed’s up-and-coming therapy zoldonrasib.
RevMed is also running two other Phase 3 trials of Rasonque, RASolute 304 in the adjuvant setting and RASolute 305 in first-line, as well as studying the drug in non-small cell lung cancer, where RAS mutations drive disease. Zoldonrasib, meanwhile, is also under investigation in colorectal cancer.
RevMed has key clinical development partnerships with BeOne Medicines and Summit Therapeutics underway as well, featuring Rasonque and other pipeline assets.
“Rasonque’s approval and launch mark a monumental step forward for patients living with RAS-dependent cancers and open an important new chapter for Revolution Medicines,” Goldsmith said. “With this momentum, we continue our deep commitment to discovering, developing and delivering innovative targeted medicines with the urgency patients deserve.”
